leader.name: Hibatullah Akhundzada
leader.title: Supreme Leader
leader.bio: Hibatullah Akhundzada is an Afghan politician and cleric who is serving as the supreme leader of Afghanistan under the Taliban government. He has led the Taliban since 2016, and came to power with its victory over U.S.-backed forces in the 2001–2021 war. A highly reclusive figure, he has almost no digital footprint except for two photographs and several audio recordings of speeches. Head of government: Hasan Akhund.

4.overview: Afghanistan's central issue is its unresolved conflict with Pakistan, which it disputes over the Durand Line, the colonial-era border that the Taliban government does not recognise as settled, and over cross-border militancy. Internally, the Taliban face an active insurgency from the Islamic State in Khorasan Province and resistance groups. The Taliban government relies on Pakistan, Iran, China and Qatar for trade, diplomacy and support, while Iran's water-sharing and border disputes with Afghanistan add further strain.

leader.name: Edi Rama
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Edvin Kristaq "Edi" Rama is an Albanian politician, artist, writer, and former professional basketball player who has served as prime minister of Albania since 2013 and as chairman of the Socialist Party of Albania since 2005. He was the Minister of Culture, Youth and Sports from 1998 to 2000 and the Mayor of Tirana from 2000 to 2011. Head of state: Bajram Begaj.

8.overview: Albania's position is shaped less by territorial disputes than by its neighbours and alliances: its western security rests on NATO membership and close ties with the United States, Italy and Turkey, while its relationship with Kosovo is among its closest bonds. Greece is a sensitive neighbour, with the Albanian and Greek governments having long disputed maritime boundaries in the Ionian and Adriatic seas. Migration flows across the Adriatic from Italy and Greece remain a practical concern.

leader.name: Abdelmadjid Tebboune
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Abdelmadjid Tebboune is an Algerian politician currently serving as President and Minister of National Defense of Algeria since 2019. Since the death of Liamine Zéroual in 2026, Tebboune is the only living Algerian president. Tebboune was elected in the 2019 Algerian presidential election. Head of government: Sifi Ghrieb.

12.overview: Algeria's central geopolitical issue is its rivalry with Morocco over Western Sahara, where Algeria backs the Polisario Front and its claim to an independent Sahrawi state, while Morocco claims the territory as its own. The two countries have also been at odds over their shared border, which has remained closed for years. Algeria relies on Russia for defence equipment and on Italy and China for trade and investment, while its substantial oil and gas exports to Europe give it significant economic leverage.

16.overview: American Samoa has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its position is shaped mainly by its status as an unincorporated U.S. territory in the South Pacific. Its defence, foreign relations and largely its economy depend on the United States, and its tuna canning industry and U.S. federal funding are its main sources of economic leverage. Neighbouring Samoa, to the west, is its closest cultural and political counterpart, while regional ties run through the Pacific Islands Forum.

leader.name: Xavier Espot Zamora
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Xavier Espot Zamora is an Andorran judge and politician who has served as Prime Minister of Andorra and President of the Democrats for Andorra since 2019. He previously served as Minister of Social Affairs, Justice, and the Interior from 2012 to 2019. A trained lawyer, Espot began his professional career as a court clerk and later served as a judge in various sections of the Andorran judiciary. Head of state: Emmanuel Macron.

20.overview: Andorra has no territorial disputes or active security threats, and its borders with France and Spain are settled and uncontested. Its position is shaped by its small size and deep economic ties to its two larger neighbours, which supply its trade, transport links and tourism. Its security is largely handled through its close relationship with France and Spain, which are co-princes of the state.

leader.name: João Lourenço
leader.title: President
leader.bio: João Manuel Gonçalves Lourençoˈɾẽ.su]; born 5 March 1954) is an Angolan politician who is currently serving as the third president of Angola since 26 September 2017. Previously, he was the minister of defence from 2014 to 2017. In September 2018, he became the chairman of the People's Movement for the Liberation of Angola, the ruling party.

24.overview: Angola's geopolitical position is shaped less by territorial disputes than by its oil wealth and regional ties. Its main external partners are Portugal, its former colonial power, and China, which is a major lender and buyer of Angolan crude. Angola is a central player in Southern African diplomacy through the African Union and the Southern African Development Community, and its borders with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Namibia are a practical focus for cooperation and security. Its relationship with South Africa remains important for trade and regional stability.

leader.name: Gaston Browne
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Gaston Alphonso Browne is an Antiguan politician serving as the prime minister of Antigua and Barbuda and leader of the Labour Party since 2014. Before entering politics, he was a banker and businessman. Head of state: Charles III.

28.overview: Antigua and Barbuda has no significant territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its small size and reliance on partners. It is a member of the Organisation of American States, the Commonwealth and CARICOM, and depends on regional cooperation, tourism and external aid. Its foreign policy is influenced by larger powers in the Caribbean, particularly the United States and the United Kingdom, and by its exposure to hurricanes and climate change.

leader.name: Ilham Aliyev
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Ilham Heydar oghlu Aliyev is an Azerbaijani politician and statesman who has been the fourth president of Azerbaijan since 2003. He is the son of the previous president, Heydar Aliyev, and has led the New Azerbaijan Party since 2005. Aliyev briefly served as prime minister for his father before being elected to office in a presidential election defined by irregularities, shortly before his father's death. Head of government: Ali Asadov.

31.overview: Azerbaijan's central geopolitical issue is its long dispute with Armenia over Nagorno-Karabakh, a region internationally recognized as Azerbaijani but controlled by ethnic Armenian forces until Azerbaijan regained it in 2023. Relations with Armenia remain strained, and the two sides still contest the terms of a lasting peace. Azerbaijan relies on Turkey as its closest ally, along with Israel, Pakistan, Georgia and Kazakhstan, and uses its oil and gas exports and pipelines to Europe and Turkey for leverage.

leader.name: Javier Milei
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Javier Gerardo Milei is an Argentine politician and economist who has served as the president of Argentina since 2023. He previously served as a member of the Chamber of Deputies from 2021 to 2023.

32.overview: Argentina's most enduring geopolitical issue is its claim to the Falkland Islands (Malvinas), which the United Kingdom administers and which Argentina considers occupied territory, along with the South Georgia and South Sandwich Islands. Argentina also claims a sector of Antarctica that overlaps with British and Chilean claims. Its foreign policy relies on Mercosur ties with Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay and Chile, and on partnerships with the United States and Spain, while its large agricultural and energy resources give it trade leverage in regional and global markets.

leader.name: Anthony Albanese
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Anthony Norman Albanese is an Australian politician who has served as the 31st prime minister of Australia since 2022. He has been the leader of the Labor Party since 2019 and the member of Parliament for the New South Wales division of Grayndler since 1996. Born in Sydney, Albanese attended St Mary's Cathedral College and studied economics at the University of Sydney. Head of state: Peter Cosgrove.

36.overview: Australia's central strategic concern is the rise of China, which it sees as a major rival and the main driver of its defence planning, particularly around the South China Sea and the security of Taiwan. Australia has no territorial disputes with its neighbours and relies heavily on its alliances with the United States and United Kingdom through AUKUS, the Five Eyes intelligence partnership, and the Quad with the United States, Japan and India. Its economy depends on Chinese demand for iron ore and coal, a trade exposure that shapes its careful diplomacy.

leader.name: Christian Stocker
leader.title: Chancellor
leader.bio: Christian Stocker is an Austrian politician who has served as chancellor of Austria since March 2025. A member of the People's Party, he has been a member of the National Council since 2019 and Chair of the People's Party since 5 January 2025. He had previously served as general secretary of the party from September 2022 to January 2025. Head of state: Alexander Van der Bellen.

40.overview: Austria has no territorial disputes or active rivalries, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its neighbours and its place in Europe. As a neutral EU member with a constitutional commitment to neutrality, it avoids military alliances and relies on the European Union and close ties with Germany, Italy, Switzerland, Hungary, Czechia and Slovenia. Migration routes through the Balkans and Central Europe, and Russia's energy leverage over European gas supplies, are its main external pressures.

leader.name: Philip Davis (Bahamian politician)
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Philip Edward Davis is a Bahamian lawyer and politician who has served as the fifth prime minister of The Bahamas since 2021. He served as minister of finance from 2021 to 2026. He has led the Progressive Liberal Party since 2017 and has represented Cat Island, Rum Cay & San Salvador in the House of Assembly since 2002, having previously held the seat from 1992 to 1997. Head of state: Charles III.

44.overview: The Bahamas has no active territorial disputes or armed rivalries, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its neighbours and partners. Its proximity to the United States and the Florida Straits makes migration, maritime security and drug trafficking the key concerns. It relies on close ties with the United States and the United Kingdom, and its tourism and financial-services economy depends on regional stability and climate resilience.

leader.name: Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Salman bin Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa has been the Crown Prince of Bahrain since 1999, and the Prime Minister of Bahrain since 2020. He previously served as the Commander-in-Chief of the Bahrain Defence Force from 1999 to 2008. Head of state: Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa.

48.overview: Bahrain's central geopolitical concern is its position across from Iran in the Gulf, where it hosts a US Navy Fifth Fleet presence and relies on Saudi Arabia for security backing, notably through the causeway linking the two states. Bahrain's dependence on the Strait of Hormuz for its oil and trade exposes it to regional tensions between Iran and the Gulf monarchies. It is also a close partner of the United States and the United Kingdom, and a member of the GCC.

leader.name: Tarique Rahman
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Tarique Rahman, also known as Tarique Zia, is a Bangladeshi politician who has served as the prime minister of Bangladesh and chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party since 2026. He is the eldest son of former President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia. Born in 1968, Rahman rose to prominence in the Bangladesh Nationalist Party during Khaleda Zia's premiership. Head of state: Mohammed Shahabuddin.

50.overview: Bangladesh's central geopolitical concern is its shared border with India, where the two governments have worked through long-running disputes over enclaves, river water sharing and border security. Its position is shaped by the Ganges and Brahmaputra river systems that both countries depend on, by its vulnerability to flooding and migration pressures from Myanmar's Rakhine State, and by its growing economic ties with China. It draws diplomatic and development support from Japan, the United States and the United Kingdom.

leader.name: Nikol Pashinyan
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Nikol Vovayi Pashinyan is an Armenian politician who has served as the 16th and current prime minister of Armenia since 2018. A journalist by profession, Pashinyan founded his own newspaper in 1998, which was shut down a year later for libel. He was sentenced for one year for defamation against then Minister of National Security Serzh Sargsyan. Head of state: Vahagn Khachaturyan.

51.overview: Armenia's central geopolitical issue is its unresolved conflict with Azerbaijan over Nagorno-Karabakh, which Armenia long backed and which Azerbaijan reclaimed by force in 2023, after which most ethnic Armenians fled the region. The two countries also dispute their closed border and the delimitation of their frontier. Armenia relies on Russia for security through the CSTO and the EAEU, maintains ties with Iran, and has been drawing closer to France and India for arms and diplomatic support.

leader.name: Mia Mottley
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Prime minister of Barbados since 2018. Head of state: Sandra Mason.

52.overview: Barbados has no territorial disputes, armed conflicts, or declared adversaries, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its size and regional ties. As a small Caribbean island state, it relies on CARICOM partners such as Trinidad and Tobago and Jamaica, as well as its Commonwealth and OAS memberships and longstanding ties with the United Kingdom. Its main external pressures are economic and environmental, including trade exposure, tourism dependence, and vulnerability to hurricanes and rising sea levels.

leader.name: Bart De Wever
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Bart Albert Liliane De Wever, also known as BDW, is a Belgian politician who has served as the Prime Minister of Belgium since February 2025. From 2004 to 2025, De Wever had been the leader of the New Flemish Alliance, a political party advocating Flemish independence. From January 2013 to February 2025, he was Mayor of Antwerp, following the 2012 municipal elections. Head of state: Philippe of Belgium.

56.overview: Belgium has no territorial disputes or active rivalries, so its geopolitical position is shaped by its place at the heart of Europe. It depends on NATO and the European Union, hosts Brussels as the seat of both institutions, and works closely with the Netherlands, Luxembourg, France, Germany and the United Kingdom. Its security role centres on NATO, including the US nuclear weapons stationed at Kleine Brogel airbase.

60.overview: Bermuda has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its position is shaped chiefly by its status as a British Overseas Territory, with the United Kingdom responsible for defence and foreign affairs. Its key external relationships are with the United Kingdom and the United States, the latter a close partner on security and finance. As a small island economy dependent on international business and tourism, it is especially exposed to global financial regulation and tax transparency rules, and to hurricanes and rising sea levels.

leader.name: Tshering Tobgay
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Tshering Tobgay is a Bhutanese politician who is the seventh prime minister of Bhutan since 2024, having previously held the office from 2013 to 2018. Tobgay is the leader of the People's Democratic Party, and was also the Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly from March 2008 to April 2013. Head of state: Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck.

64.overview: Bhutan's central geopolitical issue is its long-running border dispute with China, which has no diplomatic relations with Bhutan and whose claims cover areas in the north and west, including around the Doklam plateau near the Indian border. Bhutan relies heavily on India for security, trade, energy and development aid, and its foreign policy is closely tied to New Delhi's interests. Bangladesh is a further partner, and Bhutan's position is shaped by the Himalayan geography that separates it from its two giant neighbours.

leader.name: Rodrigo Paz
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Rodrigo Paz Pereira is a Bolivian politician and diplomat who has served as the 68th president of Bolivia since 2025. The eldest son of former president Jaime Paz Zamora and great-nephew of president Víctor Paz Estenssoro, he served as a senator for Tarija from 2020 to 2025.

68.overview: Bolivia's central geopolitical issue is its landlocked status, which it has long contested with Chile after losing its Pacific coastline in the 1879-1884 War of the Pacific, and it pursued the matter through international courts. Its relations with Chile remain shaped by that loss, while it relies on Peru for port access and on Argentina and Brazil as key trade and energy partners. Its regional alignment runs through the OAS and Mercosur, and its lithium reserves give it growing strategic weight.

leader.name: Borjana Krišto
leader.title: Chairman
leader.bio: Borjana Krišto is a Bosnian Croat politician who has served as Chairwoman of the Council of Ministers of Bosnia and Herzegovina since January 2023. She previously served as president of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 2007 to 2011. She is the first woman to hold both positions. Head of state: Željko Komšić.

70.overview: Bosnia and Herzegovina's central issue is its fragile internal political order, shaped by the 1995 Dayton settlement, which divided the country between the Bosniak-Croat Federation and the Serb-led Republika Srpska, a arrangement that Republika Srpska leaders have repeatedly threatened to unwind. The country relies on the European Union and the United States for oversight and security, and it looks to neighbouring Croatia and Serbia, along with Turkey, Slovenia and Austria, for trade, political ties and influence.

leader.name: Duma Boko
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of Botswana.

72.overview: Botswana has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its position is shaped chiefly by its neighbours and the economic weight of its diamond trade. Its relations with South Africa, Namibia, Zimbabwe and Zambia are central to regional trade, water and migration, while membership in the African Union, the Commonwealth and the Southern African Development Community anchors its diplomacy.

leader.name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known mononymously as Lula, is a Brazilian politician, trade unionist and former metalworker who has served as president of Brazil since 2023 and from 2003 to 2011. He is a member of the Workers' Party. Born in Pernambuco, Lula quit school after second grade to work, and did not learn to read until he was ten years old.

76.overview: Brazil has no active territorial disputes or armed rivalries with neighbours, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its regional leadership and its major partners. It anchors South American diplomacy through Mercosur and works with Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay on trade and regional security. Its relations with China and the United States, the two leading external powers in its economy and foreign policy, are central to its strategy, and Brazil's large Amazon region draws international attention on climate and sovereignty.

leader.name: Johnny Briceño
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: John Antonio Briceño is a Belizean politician who has served as the fifth and current prime minister of Belize since 2020 and the leader of the People's United Party since 2016. He was Leader of the Opposition from 2008 to 2011 and from 2016 to 2020. From 1998 to 2007, he served as the deputy prime minister under Prime Minister Said Musa. Head of state: Charles III.

84.overview: Belize's central geopolitical issue is its long-running territorial claim against Guatemala, which has contested Belize's sovereignty and its southern border for decades, with the dispute still pending before the International Court of Justice. Belize relies on the United Kingdom, whose military presence and security ties have long deterred the claim, and on Mexico and CARICOM partners for regional support. Its position is also shaped by its small size and exposure to regional migration and trade flows.

leader.name: Jeremiah Manele
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Jeremiah Manele is a Solomon Islands politician who served as prime minister of Solomon Islands between 2024 and 2026. He was the first prime minister of the country to come from Isabel Province. Head of state: Charles III.

90.overview: The Solomon Islands' main geopolitical concern is its strategic position in the South Pacific, where it has been drawn into rivalry between Australia and China over regional influence. Its 2019 switch of diplomatic recognition from Taiwan to China and a 2022 security pact with Beijing reflect this competition. The country relies on Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea for security, policing and aid, and on the Commonwealth and the Pacific Islands Forum for regional diplomacy.

92.overview: The US Virgin Islands are an unincorporated territory of the United States, so their geopolitical position is shaped by that status rather than by any contested border. Their main external concerns are hurricanes and climate-driven storms, which shape disaster response and reliance on federal aid, along with regional migration and Caribbean trade links. Security and foreign policy are handled by Washington, which provides defence and governs the territory's international relations.

leader.name: Hassanal Bolkiah
leader.title: Sultan
leader.bio: Hassanal Bolkiah Muiz'zaddin Wad'daulah has reigned as the sultan of Brunei since 1967, and has also served as the prime minister of Brunei since its independence from British rule in 1984. He is among the world's few remaining absolute monarchs.

96.overview: Brunei's position is shaped less by disputes than by its small size and neighbours. It shares the island of Borneo with Malaysia, which surrounds the sultanate's territory, and it holds a maritime claim in the South China Sea that overlaps with China's nine-dash line, though it has kept this issue low-key. Brunei relies on its ASEAN membership, close ties with Singapore and Indonesia, and the British Gurkha presence that has long underpinned its defence, while its oil and gas revenues give it economic weight.

leader.name: Kiril Petkov
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Kiril Petkov Petkov is a Bulgarian politician, economist, and entrepreneur, who served as Prime Minister of Bulgaria from December 2021 to August 2022. He was the co-founder of We Continue the Change, a political party, alongside Assen Vassilev. Petkov was born in Plovdiv, but grew up in Sofia and was educated by his parents, who were both teachers. Head of state: Iliana Iotova.

100.overview: Bulgaria's geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its Black Sea coastline and its place on NATO's and the EU's southeastern flank, close to the Russia-Ukraine war and the Black Sea security environment. It has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours. Its dependence on Russian energy has been a major strategic issue, and it relies on NATO allies, particularly the United States, along with Romania, Greece and Turkey for regional security and trade routes.

leader.name: Myint Swe
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Myint Swe was a Burmese politician and army officer who served as the third first vice president of Myanmar from 2016 until his death in 2025. A member of the Union Solidarity and Development Party, Myint Swe served as acting president of Myanmar in 2018 and again from 2021 to 2025. Head of government: Min Aung Hlaing.

104.overview: Myanmar's central geopolitical issue is its internal conflict, with the military government fighting a wide range of ethnic armed organisations and newer resistance forces in the Shan, Kachin, Karen and Rakhine regions. Its border areas with China, Thailand and India are shaped by this fighting, and cross-border trade in minerals, timber and drugs gives armed groups leverage. Myanmar relies heavily on China and Russia for diplomatic cover and arms, while ASEAN engagement remains limited.

leader.name: Évariste Ndayishimiye
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of Burundi. Head of government: Gervais Ndirakobuca.

108.overview: Burundi's most significant geopolitical concern is its tense relationship with Rwanda, whose border has been closed for years amid mutual accusations of supporting rebel groups. Its ties to neighbouring Tanzania, Rwanda and Kenya are shaped by shared regional security and trade within the East African Community, while Burundi also depends on African Union frameworks and aid for stability. The lingering effects of its civil war and ethnic tensions keep internal security a central preoccupation.

leader.name: Alexander Lukashenko
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Alexander Grigoryevich Lukashenko is a Belarusian politician who has been the first and only president of Belarus since the office's establishment in 1994, making him the current longest-tenured European president. Lukashenko was born in Kopys. After graduating from what is now the Mogilev State A. Head of government: Alexander Turchin.

112.overview: Belarus's central geopolitical issue is its close dependence on Russia, which underpins its security, economy and political survival, leaving it largely aligned with Moscow against the West. Its relations with neighbouring Poland, Lithuania and Ukraine are strained, with border closures and mutual accusations over migration, sanctions and military activity. Belarus also leans on China and Kazakhstan for trade and diplomatic support, and is a member of the CSTO, EAEU and SCO.

leader.name: Hun Manet
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Hun Manet is a Cambodian politician and military officer who has served as Prime Minister of Cambodia and Vice President of the ruling Cambodian People's Party since 2023. He is the second child of Senate president and former prime minister Hun Sen and Bun Rany. Manet grew up in Phnom Penh, where he received his general education before joining the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces in 1995. Head of state: Norodom Sihamoni.

116.overview: Cambodia's central geopolitical issue is its long-running border dispute with Thailand, including disputed areas around the Preah Vihear temple and other stretches of frontier that have produced armed clashes. It also relies heavily on China for investment, aid and diplomatic cover, while maintaining close ties with Vietnam and Laos as neighbours and members of ASEAN.

leader.name: Paul Biya
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Paul Barthélemy Biya is a Cameroonian politician who has been serving as the second president of Cameroon since 1982. He was previously the fifth prime minister under President Ahmadou Ahidjo from 1975 to 1982. Head of government: Joseph Ngute.

120.overview: Cameroon's central geopolitical challenge is the Anglophone crisis in its North-West and South-West regions, where separatist groups seek an independent state of "Ambazonia" and fighting with government forces has displaced large numbers of people. Its northern frontier with Nigeria, including the Bakassi Peninsula, has been a longstanding border dispute, and Boko Haram violence spills across the Lake Chad basin from Nigeria. Cameroon leans on the African Union, the Commonwealth and its neighbours Chad, the Central African Republic, Equatorial Guinea and Nigeria for regional security cooperation.

leader.name: Mark Carney
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Mark Joseph Carney is a Canadian politician and economist who is the 24th prime minister of Canada and leader of the Liberal Party, serving since 2025. Carney has been the member of Parliament for Nepean since his election in April 2025. He was previously Governor of the Bank of Canada from 2008 to 2013 and Governor of the Bank of England from 2013 to 2020. Head of state: Charles III.

124.overview: Canada's geopolitical position is shaped less by territorial disputes than by its relationship with the United States, its largest trading partner and closest security ally, which shapes trade, defence, and Arctic cooperation. Canada has no major active border dispute, though its Arctic sovereignty claims overlap with those of Denmark over Hans Island and with the United States over the Northwest Passage and Beaufort Sea. As a NATO and Five Eyes member, it leans on Western alliances and is a G7 and G20 partner.

leader.name: José Maria Neves
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Cape Verdean politician and former prime minister of Cape Verde. Head of government: Francisco Carvalho.

132.overview: Cabo Verde has no territorial disputes or active rivalries, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its small size, its Atlantic location, and its ties to former colonial power Portugal and to regional neighbour Senegal. Its key external relationships run through the African Union and ECOWAS, with Europe a major source of aid, investment and migration links. Its exposure to climate pressures, dependence on tourism and remittances, and strategic position on Atlantic shipping routes are its main external vulnerabilities.

136.overview: The Cayman Islands is a British Overseas Territory with no territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its constitutional tie to the United Kingdom, which handles its defence and foreign affairs. Its economy depends on financial services, tourism and close links with the United States and Caribbean neighbours, and its exposure to hurricanes and sea-level rise is a major long-term concern.

leader.name: Faustin-Archange Touadéra
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Faustin-Archange Touadéra is a Central African politician and mathematician who has been president of the Central African Republic since March 2016, and was previously its prime minister from 2008 to 2013. He was elected to the presidency at the 2015–16 general election, in a second round of voting against former prime minister Anicet Georges Dologuélé. Head of government: Félix Moloua.

140.overview: The Central African Republic's central problem is internal: a long-running armed conflict between the government and rebel and militia groups, with much of the countryside outside state control. Its position is shaped by its landlocked location and reliance on neighbours Chad, Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of the Congo for trade routes and security cooperation. Russia has become a significant security partner, and the country draws on African Union support.

leader.name: Anura Kumara Dissanayake
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of Sri Lanka since 2024. Head of government: Harini Amarasuriya.

144.overview: Sri Lanka's main geopolitical issues are less about territorial disputes than about its position on Indian Ocean sea lanes and the rivalry between India and China for influence there. Its ports, including Hambantota and Colombo, have drawn Chinese investment and debt concerns, while India views the island as a core security interest. Sri Lanka relies on India, China and Japan for aid, trade and investment, and its own sovereign debt crisis has left it heavily dependent on outside financing.

leader.name: Mahamat Déby
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Military leader of Chad since 2021.

148.overview: Chad's central concern is the spillover of conflict from its neighbours, especially Sudan's war along its eastern border, which has drawn in refugees and armed groups and strained the Chad-Sudan frontier. Its northern Tibesti region has seen longstanding rebel activity, and Boko Haram and other armed groups threaten the Lake Chad basin shared with Cameroon, Niger and Nigeria. Chad relies on France for military support and on regional security cooperation, while its oil exports, routed through Cameroon, give it some leverage.

leader.name: José Antonio Kast
leader.title: President
leader.bio: José Antonio Kast Rist is a Chilean lawyer and politician who has served as the 38th president of Chile since 2026. Kast previously served as a member of the Chamber of Deputies from 2002 to 2018, representing districts in the Santiago Metropolitan Region. Born in Santiago to a German immigrant family, Kast graduated from the Pontificial Catholic University of Chile in 1990 with a degree in law.

152.overview: Chile's most significant longstanding issue is its maritime boundary with Peru, which was settled by the International Court of Justice in 2014 after a dispute over the Pacific waters, and its border with Bolivia, which lost its access to the sea to Chile in the 19th-century War of the Pacific and still seeks sovereign access. Chile relies on regional partnerships with Argentina, Peru, Brazil and the United States, and its copper, lithium and other mineral exports give it considerable economic leverage in global markets.

leader.name: Xi Jinping
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Xi Jinping is a Chinese politician who is the paramount leader of China. He has served as the general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and chairman of the Party Central Military Commission since 2012, and as the president of China and chairman of the State Central Military Commission since 2013. The elder son of Xi Zhongxun's second marriage to Qi Xin, Xi was born in Beijing. Head of government: Li Qiang.

156.overview: China claims Taiwan as its territory and has not ruled out force to take it, making the Taiwan Strait its central flashpoint. It contests much of the South China Sea with the Philippines, Vietnam and others, and has an unresolved Himalayan border with India, all amid strategic rivalry with the United States. Beijing leans on partners such as Russia, Pakistan and North Korea, and wields leverage through its dominance of rare-earth supply chains.

158.unSeat: Not a UN member — represented by the PRC since 1971

leader.name: Lai Ching-te
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Lai Ching-te, also known as William Lai, is a Taiwanese politician, physician, and nephrologist who has served as the 8th president of the Republic of China since 2024. A member of the Democratic Progressive Party, he has been the party's chairman since 2023. Born in Wanli District, New Taipei, Lai studied medicine at National Taiwan University and National Cheng Kung University. Head of government: Wu Den-yih.

158.overview: China claims Taiwan as its territory and has not ruled out force to bring it under its control, making the Taiwan Strait the central flashpoint in the region. Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's claim and manages the risk with support from the United States, its main security partner, alongside Japan, the Philippines and Australia. Taiwan's semiconductor industry gives it significant economic weight and leverage in global supply chains.

leader.name: Abelardo de la Espriella
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Abelardo Gabriel de la Espriella Otero is a Colombian lawyer, businessman, and politician who has served as the 36th president of Colombia since 2026. He is the founder and leader of the far-right Defenders of the Homeland party, established initially as a movement in 2024.

170.overview: Colombia's central security challenge is internal: decades of conflict with armed groups, including remnants of the FARC and the ELN, and the drug trade that funds them, shape its politics and its border with Venezuela. Its relationship with Venezuela, including disputes over migration, smuggling and the border, is a persistent source of tension. Colombia relies heavily on the United States for security and counternarcotics cooperation, and maintains close ties with Brazil, Peru and Ecuador.

leader.name: Azali Assoumani
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of Comoros.

174.overview: The Comoros' central geopolitical issue is the status of Mayotte, a French-administered island that the Comoros claims as part of its territory and that France has retained since the archipelago's independence in 1975. The dispute remains unresolved and shapes relations with Paris, which is also the Comoros' principal partner for aid and security. Madagascar is a close regional neighbour, and the country relies on African Union, SADC and Arab League membership for diplomatic backing.

leader.name: Denis Sassou Nguesso
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of the Republic of the Congo. Head of government: Anatole Collinet Makosso.

178.overview: The Republic of the Congo has no major territorial disputes or active armed rivalries with neighbours, so its position is shaped mainly by its oil wealth and regional ties. As an OPEC member, its oil exports give it economic leverage, and it works closely with Gabon, Cameroon and Angola within Central African and African Union frameworks. France remains its most important outside partner, while its border with the much larger Democratic Republic of the Congo across the Congo River shapes regional security and migration concerns.

leader.name: Félix Tshisekedi
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Head of government: Sylvestre Ilunga.

180.overview: The DR Congo's central geopolitical issue is its conflict with Rwanda, which it accuses of backing the M23 rebel group in the eastern provinces of North Kivu and South Kivu, a charge Rwanda denies. Rivalries with Uganda and Burundi over border security and armed groups compound the instability, and the country relies on partners such as Angola, Zambia and the African Union and SADC for diplomatic backing. Its vast reserves of cobalt, copper and coltan give it considerable leverage in global supply chains.

leader.name: Laura Fernández
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Laura Virginia Fernández Delgado is a Costa Rican politician and political scientist who has served as the president of Costa Rica since 2026. As the presidential candidate of the Sovereign People's Party, Fernández won the 2026 presidential election. She previously served as the minister of national planning and economic policy from 2022 to 2025, as well as the minister of the presidency from 2024 to 2025.

188.overview: Costa Rica has no major territorial disputes or armed rivalries, so its position is shaped by its neighbours and partners rather than by contested borders. Its relations with Nicaragua are its most sensitive regional issue, marked by migration flows and periodic friction over border management. Costa Rica relies on the United States for security cooperation and trade, works closely with Panama, and is a long-standing member of the Organization of American States.

leader.name: Andrej Plenković
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Andrej Plenković is a Croatian politician who has served as prime minister of Croatia since 2016. He is the leader of the Croatian Democratic Union, serving since 2016. Plenković is the longest-serving Croatian prime minister. Head of state: Zoran Milanović.

191.overview: Croatia's main geopolitical concern is its long-running maritime and border questions with its neighbours, notably the unresolved sea boundary with Slovenia in the Bay of Piran and the land and maritime frontier with Bosnia and Herzegovina, including disputes over the Prevlaka peninsula and parts of the Adriatic. Its position is shaped by its membership of NATO and the European Union, close ties with Germany, Austria and the United States, and the influence of Balkan migration routes and regional stability.

leader.name: Miguel Díaz-Canel
leader.title: President
leader.bio: First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba and top leader of Cuba since 2021. Head of government: Manuel Marrero Cruz.

192.overview: Cuba's central geopolitical fact is its long rivalry with the United States, which has maintained an embargo and sanctions for decades and sits just 90 miles across the Florida Straits. Havana relies on Venezuela, Russia and Nicaragua for political backing and on Venezuelan oil, while Mexico is a key trading partner and migration route. Its position is shaped mainly by this U.S. pressure and by the support of these partners rather than by any territorial dispute.

leader.name: Nikos Christodoulides
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Nikos Christodoulides is a Cypriot politician, diplomat, and academic who has served as the 8th President of Cyprus since 2023. He previously served as Government Spokesman from 2014 to 2018 and Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2018 to 2022, both under his predecessor Nicos Anastasiades. Head of government: Nicos Anastasiades.

196.overview: Cyprus's central issue is the division of the island since Turkey's 1974 military intervention, with the Turkish Cypriot north occupied and recognised only by Turkey, and the Greek Cypriot Republic of Cyprus controlling the south. Turkey remains its principal rival, and maritime disputes over offshore gas fields and exclusive economic zones with Turkey and Turkey-backed claims in the east Mediterranean keep tensions alive. Cyprus relies on Greece, France, Israel and Egypt for security and energy cooperation, and on EU membership for its diplomatic weight.

leader.name: Andrej Babiš
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Andrej Babiš is a Czech politician and businessman who has been the prime minister of the Czech Republic since December 2025, having previously served as prime minister from 2017 to 2021. Prior to that, he was the minister of finance and deputy prime minister from 2014 to 2017. A populist, Babiš has led the ANO 2011 political party since he founded it in 2012. Head of state: Petr Pavel.

203.overview: The Czech Republic has no territorial disputes or active rivalries, so its position is shaped by its place in Europe. It is a firm member of NATO and the European Union and relies on those alliances for its security, with Germany and Poland as close partners within the region. Its main external pressures are migration and energy supply, and it works with Slovakia, Austria and Hungary on shared regional concerns.

leader.name: Romuald Wadagni
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of Benin. Head of government: Patrice Talon.

204.overview: Benin's main geopolitical concerns are regional rather than territorial: jihadist violence spilling over from the Sahel into its northern border zone with Burkina Faso and Niger, and the security of its border with Nigeria, which is also its key economic partner. Benin has no major disputed borders or frozen conflicts. It relies on ECOWAS and the African Union for regional security cooperation, and on France for military and development ties.

208.overview: Denmark's central security concern is Russia, which it regards as the main threat to the Baltic Sea region and to Arctic stability, with Greenland's strategic position and its dispute-free but sensitive Arctic waters drawing attention from Russia and the United States. Denmark relies heavily on NATO and its alliance with the United States, and works closely with Sweden, Norway, Finland and Germany on regional defence.

leader.name: Roosevelt Skerrit
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Roosevelt Skerrit, also known as "Roozey" or "Skerro", is a Dominican politician who has been Prime Minister of Dominica since 2004; he has also been the Member of Parliament for the Vieille Case constituency since 2000. Regionally, he has served as the chairman of the Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States and, most recently, as chairman of the Caribbean Community in 2010 and 2023. Head of state: Sylvanie Burton.

212.overview: Dominica has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its small size and vulnerability to hurricanes and climate change. It relies on regional bodies such as CARICOM, the Organisation of American States and the Commonwealth, and on aid and cooperation from partners including the United States, the United Kingdom and Taiwan. Its exposure to migration pressure and trade dependence on its larger Caribbean neighbours also influence its foreign policy.

leader.name: Luis Abinader
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Luis Rodolfo Abinader Corona is a Dominican economist, businessman, and politician who has served as the 54th president of the Dominican Republic since 2020. He was the Modern Revolutionary Party candidate for President of the Dominican Republic in the 2016, 2020, and 2024 general elections. He is the president of his party since 5 September 2026.

214.overview: The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti, and migration, border control and cross-border tensions with its western neighbour are its most persistent strategic concerns. Its security relationship is closely tied to the United States, its largest trade and security partner, and it works within the Organization of American States. Caribbean drug-trafficking routes also make cooperation with US and regional law enforcement a core feature of its policy.

leader.name: Daniel Noboa
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Daniel Roy Gilchrist Noboa Azín is an Ecuadorian politician and businessman serving as the 48th and current president of Ecuador since 2023. Having first taken office at the age of 35, he is the second-youngest president in the country's history, after Juan José Flores, and the youngest to be elected.

218.overview: Ecuador's main geopolitical concern is its long-running border dispute with Peru, which was largely settled by a 1998 peace agreement, though the frontier remains sensitive. Its most pressing security pressures come from Colombia, where armed groups and drug trafficking spill across the northern border. Ecuador relies on Colombia, Peru and the United States for security and trade cooperation, and works within the Organization of American States.

leader.name: Nayib Bukele
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Nayib Armando Bukele Ortez is a Salvadoran politician who has served as the 43rd president of El Salvador since 2019. In 1999, Bukele established an advertising company and worked at another owned by his father, Armando Bukele Kattán. Both companies advertised election campaigns for the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front political party.

222.overview: El Salvador has no major territorial dispute or armed conflict with a neighbour, and its border with Honduras and Guatemala is settled. Its security concerns are internal, centred on organised gang violence, with migration and regional security cooperation shaping policy. It relies on the United States as its key partner for aid, trade and migration ties, and on Guatemala and Honduras in the Central American regional framework, with the Organization of American States as its main multilateral forum.

leader.name: Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Equatoguinean politician, President of Equatorial Guinea since 1979. Head of government: Manuel Osa Nsue Nsua.

226.overview: Equatorial Guinea's main longstanding issue is a maritime and territorial dispute with neighbouring Gabon over the Mbanié, Cocotiers and Conga islets in the Gulf of Guinea, which Gabon and Equatorial Guinea both claim. The country relies on regional partners Cameroon and Gabon, on former colonial power Spain, and on African Union membership. Its position is shaped mainly by oil revenue, its OPEC membership, and the influence of larger external energy investors.

leader.name: Abiy Ahmed
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Abiy Ahmed Ali is an Ethiopian politician and former military officer who is the current prime minister of Ethiopia since 2018. He is also the leader of the Prosperity Party since 2019. Abiy joined the rebel forces fighting against the regime of Mengistu Haile Mariam in his teens and after the collapse of the Derg in 1991, became a Lieutenant Colonel in the Ethiopian National Defense Force. Head of state: Taye Atske Selassie.

231.overview: Ethiopia's central geopolitical issue is its long-running rivalry with Eritrea, a legacy of the 1998–2000 border war and an unresolved boundary dispute, which has left the two countries in a tense standoff. Ethiopia also faces a difficult relationship with Egypt over the Nile, as Addis Ababa's Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam dispute with Cairo and Khartoum over water flows remains a major strategic concern. Ethiopia relies on Djibouti for the port access that handles most of its trade, and on partners including Kenya, the United Arab Emirates and China for investment and diplomatic backing.

leader.name: Isaias Afwerki
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of Eritrea since 1993.

232.overview: Eritrea's central geopolitical issue is its unresolved border dispute with Ethiopia, which fought a costly war from 1998 to 2000 and has not fully implemented the boundary ruling, including the contested town of Badme. Relations remain tense, with Eritrea wary of Ethiopian intentions in the Horn of Africa. Eritrea has drawn closer to Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, whose Red Sea interests give it diplomatic and economic weight, while its position on the Red Sea coast keeps it strategically relevant.

leader.name: Kaja Kallas
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Kaja Kallas is an Estonian politician and diplomat. She was the first female prime minister of Estonia, a role she held from 2021 until 2024, when she resigned in advance of her appointment as High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy. Since 2024, she has served in that role as well as Vice-President of the European Commission in the second von der Leyen Commission. Head of state: Ülle Madise.

233.overview: Russia is Estonia's central security concern, shaped by a long-standing border dispute over areas near Lake Peipus and the Narva river, which Russia has not fully settled by treaty. Russian military pressure and influence in neighbouring Belarus add to the threat, and Estonia relies on NATO collective defence, the United States and the United Kingdom, alongside close cooperation with Latvia, Lithuania and Finland.

234.overview: The Faroe Islands' central geopolitical question is its constitutional relationship with Denmark, which remains part of the Danish Realm while holding wide self-government. Its position is shaped by Arctic and North Atlantic fisheries, where it manages extensive waters and negotiates access with the EU, Norway and the United Kingdom. Security is provided through Denmark and its NATO membership, and the islands' strategic relevance is linked to North Atlantic shipping and the wider Arctic.

leader.name: Sitiveni Rabuka
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Sitiveni Ligamamada Rabuka is a Fijian politician, sportsman, and former soldier who has been serving as Prime Minister of Fiji since 24 December 2022. He was the instigator of two military coups in 1987. He was democratically elected as Prime Minister of Fiji, serving from 1992 to 1999, and again in 2022, leading a three-party coalition. Head of state: Wiliame Katonivere.

242.overview: Fiji has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its security position rests on its Pacific neighbourhood and its partnerships. It depends heavily on Australia and New Zealand for defence, policing and development support, and it engages with China and other external powers. Its main strategic concerns are climate vulnerability and maintaining regional stability within the Pacific Islands Forum.

leader.name: Petteri Orpo
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Antti Petteri Orpo is a Finnish politician currently serving as the prime minister of Finland since 2023. He has also been the leader of the National Coalition Party since 2016 and briefly served as speaker of the Parliament of Finland after the 2023 parliamentary election. Head of state: Alexander Stubb.

246.overview: Finland's central security concern is its long border with Russia, which it shares across roughly 1,300 kilometres and which it views as the primary threat, shaping its decision to join NATO. Finland has no territorial disputes or frozen conflicts of its own, and its position depends on the alliance with the United States and its NATO partners, with Sweden as its closest defence partner. Its relations with the European Union and neighbouring Estonia and Norway also help shape its security and border arrangements.

nuclear.range: Intercontinental — SLBMs and air-launched cruise missiles.

leader.name: Emmanuel Macron
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Emmanuel Jean-Michel Frédéric Macron is a French politician who has served as President of France since 2017. He has been a member of Renaissance since founding the party in 2016. Macron previously served as Deputy Secretary-General to the President from 2012 to 2014 and Minister of Economics and Finance from 2014 to 2016 under President François Hollande. Head of government: Sébastien Lecornu.

250.overview: France's most serious longstanding concern is its rivalry with Russia, which it sees as a direct threat to European security, while Iran is a regional adversary. Paris relies heavily on NATO and the United States for collective defence, and works closely with Germany and the United Kingdom within the European Union. As a nuclear-armed permanent member of the UN Security Council, France also shapes global diplomacy and maintains overseas territories whose strategic and resource value gives it influence in the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.

258.overview: French Polynesia has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, but its political status is a long-running question: a sizeable independence movement, led by parties such as Tavini Huiraatira, contests its place within France, while the territory's autonomy is shaped by Paris. Its position is driven by France, its main source of funding and defence, and by the strategic interests of nuclear-armed France in the Pacific. Regional ties with Pacific Island neighbours and the influence of Chinese and US interests in the wider Pacific also shape its external environment.

leader.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of Djibouti since 1999. Head of government: Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed.

262.overview: Djibouti's central geopolitical feature is its strategic location at the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the chokepoint linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and Suez shipping routes, which hosts military bases for France, the United States, China and others. Its long-running concerns are the Afar-Somali border with neighbouring Ethiopia and Eritrea, and the tense relationship with Eritrea over the Ras Doumeira area. It relies heavily on Ethiopia for port trade and on foreign base-rental income as its economic lifeline.

leader.name: Brice Oligui Nguema
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema is a Gabonese politician and military officer who is currently serving as the fourth president of Gabon since May 2025, having previously served in this role in a transitional capacity from 2023 and was also the chairman of the Committee for the Transition and Restoration of Institutions from 2023 until his accession to the presidency. Head of government: Raymond Ndong Sima.

266.overview: Gabon has no major territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its oil wealth and its relationships with neighbours and former colonial power France. Its key partners include Cameroon, the Republic of the Congo and Equatorial Guinea, while France retains a strong military and economic presence. As an OPEC oil producer, Gabon's energy exports give it leverage in regional and global trade.

leader.name: Irakli Kobakhidze
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Irakli Kobakhidze is a Georgian politician who holds the position of the prime minister of Georgia since 2024 and chairman of Georgian Dream since 2025, having previously served in this role from 2021 to 2024. Head of state: Mikheil Kavelashvili.

268.overview: Russia is Georgia's central security concern, with Russian-backed breakaway regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia occupying about a fifth of its internationally recognised territory and Russian troops stationed there. Tbilisi's relations with Moscow remain strained, and it seeks closer ties with the West. It relies on Azerbaijan and Turkey for energy and trade routes that bypass Russia, and on Ukraine and the United States for diplomatic and security backing.

leader.name: Adama Barrow
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Adama Barrow is a Fulani Gambian politician and real estate developer who has served as third president of the Gambia since 2017. A member of the National People's Party, he has served as the party's president since its creation in 2019. Born in Mankamang Kunda, a village in Jimara district, Barrow attended Crab Island Secondary School and the Muslim High School, the latter on a scholarship.

270.overview: The Gambia has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its position is shaped mainly by its geography and regional ties. Surrounded almost entirely by Senegal, it depends on Senegalese ports, roads and cooperation for trade and movement. It is a member of the African Union, ECOWAS and the Commonwealth, and it maintains close relations with Guinea-Bissau and the United Kingdom.

leader.name: Mahmoud Abbas
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Mahmoud Rida Abbas, also known by the kunya Abu Mazen, is a Palestinian politician who has been serving as the second president of Palestine and the Palestinian National Authority since 2005. He has also been the fourth chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organization since 2004. Abbas is also a member of the Fatah party and was elected the party's chairman in 2009. Head of government: Mohammad Shtayyeh.

275.overview: Palestine's central geopolitical issue is its unresolved conflict with Israel, which occupies the West Bank and controls the Gaza Strip's borders, airspace and coastline after years of blockade and repeated wars. Palestinian claims to statehood in these territories, including East Jerusalem, remain contested and unrecognised by Israel. Palestine relies on Jordan, Egypt, Qatar and Turkey for diplomatic backing, mediation and aid, and on Arab League and OIC support in international forums.

leader.name: Friedrich Merz
leader.title: Chancellor
leader.bio: Joachim-Friedrich Martin Josef Merz is a German politician who has served as Chancellor of Germany since 6 May 2025. He has also served as Leader of the Christian Democratic Union since January 2022, leading the CDU/CSU parliamentary group as Leader of the Opposition in the Bundestag from February 2022 to May 2025. Merz was born in Brilon in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia in West Germany. Head of state: Frank-Walter Steinmeier.

276.overview: Germany's central security concern is Russia, which it sees as its principal adversary following Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, with the NATO eastern flank, including Poland, as its frontline. Germany has no territorial disputes or contested borders, and its position is shaped by its alliances, chiefly NATO and the European Union, and by reliance on the United States for nuclear deterrence through the hosting of US weapons under NATO nuclear sharing.

leader.name: John Mahama
leader.title: President
leader.bio: John Dramani Mahama is a Ghanaian politician who has been the president of the Republic of Ghana since January 2025. A member of the National Democratic Congress, he previously served as president from 2012 to 2017. Head of government: Nana Akufo-Addo.

288.overview: Ghana has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours, so its position is shaped mainly by its regional role and partnerships. It is a leading member of ECOWAS and the African Union, works closely with Nigeria, Togo, Ivory Coast and Burkina Faso, and draws on Commonwealth ties. Security concerns center on jihadist spillover from the Sahel into its northern border regions and on migration across West Africa.

292.overview: Gibraltar's central geopolitical issue is its sovereignty dispute with Spain, which claims the territory and has long sought its return, while the UK maintains that Gibraltar's people have the right to self-determination. Spain's border controls and the 2020 UK-EU framework over fishing, customs and movement remain sensitive points. Gibraltar relies on the United Kingdom for defence and foreign affairs and on its position at the Strait of Gibraltar for shipping and trade.

leader.name: Taneti Maamau
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Taneti Maamau is an I-Kiribati politician who has served as the fifth president of Kiribati since 2016. A member of the Tobwaan Kiribati Party, his policies are targeted at strengthening Kiribati's weak economy and alleviating social issues. His government announced the Kiribati Vision for 20 Years, which plans to develop the tourism and fishing industries with aid from foreign investors.

296.overview: Kiribati's main geopolitical concerns are climate change and rising sea levels, which threaten its low-lying atolls and the habitability of its islands over the long term. Its strategic position in the central Pacific draws competing interest from China and the United States, and it relies on Australia and New Zealand for aid, development support and security cooperation. It is also a member of the Pacific Islands Forum and the Commonwealth.

leader.name: Kyriakos Mitsotakis
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Kyriakos Mitsotakis is a Greek politician, and the prime minister of Greece since July 2019, except for a month between May and June 2023. Mitsotakis has been president of the New Democracy party since 2016. He is generally associated with the centre-right, espousing economically liberal policies. Head of state: Konstantinos Tasoulas.

300.overview: Greece's central dispute is with Turkey over the Aegean Sea, where the two countries contest maritime boundaries, territorial waters, and airspace, and where disputes over islets and the continental shelf have repeatedly brought tensions. The divided island of Cyprus, where Turkey maintains troops in the north, adds a further frozen conflict. Greece leans on its NATO and EU ties, close relations with Cyprus, France, the United States, Israel and Egypt, and its role in eastern Mediterranean energy routes.

304.overview: Greenland's central geopolitical question is its political future within the Kingdom of Denmark, with a long-running independence movement that has not produced a firm timetable for separation. Its strategic weight comes from its Arctic position and US Air Force presence at Pituffik Space Base, while competition for Arctic shipping routes and minerals draws in the United States, Russia and China. Greenland relies on Denmark for defence and financial support and on Iceland as a close regional partner.

leader.name: Dickon Mitchell
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Dickon Amiss Thomas Mitchell is a Grenadian politician and attorney serving as the prime minister of Grenada since 24 June 2022 and the leader of the National Democratic Congress since 2021. He led his party to victory in the 2022 general election. Head of state: Charles III.

308.overview: Grenada has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its geopolitical position is shaped by its small size and vulnerability to hurricanes, climate change and economic shocks. It relies on regional bodies such as CARICOM and the Organisation of American States, and on the Commonwealth, for trade, security cooperation and development support. Its closest external ties are with the United States and the United Kingdom, which serve as key partners for aid, trade and regional security.

316.overview: Guam is a US territory, so its security and defence posture rest on the United States, which maintains major military installations there, including Andersen Air Force Base and Naval Base Guam. Its central strategic significance lies in its position in the western Pacific, where it sits within reach of China's expanding military presence and near contested waters, and it is a key node in US plans for deterrence in the region. Guam has no territorial disputes of its own, and its political status as an unincorporated territory remains a longstanding debate among its residents.

leader.name: Bernardo Arévalo
leader.title: President
leader.bio: César Bernardo Arévalo de León is a Guatemalan diplomat, sociologist, writer, and politician who has served as the 52nd president of Guatemala since 2024. A member and co-founder of the defunct Semilla party, he previously served as a deputy in the Congress of Guatemala from 2020 to 2024, as ambassador to Spain from 1995 to 1996 and as deputy minister of foreign affairs from 1994 to 1995.

320.overview: Guatemala has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours, and its main geopolitical concerns are regional. Its position is shaped by migration flows and organised crime through Central America, and by close ties with Mexico, El Salvador and Honduras. It relies heavily on the United States for security cooperation and aid, and is a member of the Organization of American States.

leader.name: Mamady Doumbouya
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Mamadi Doumbouya is a Guinean general serving as the current fifth president of Guinea since 1 October 2021. He maintained his position after he won the 2025 Guinean presidential election in a landslide victory. Doumbouya led a coup d'état on 5 September 2021 that overthrew the previous president, Alpha Condé. Head of government: Bah Oury.

324.overview: Guinea has no major territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours, so its position is shaped mainly by regional stability and outside partnerships. Its most consequential concerns are instability in the wider West African Sahel, including the military takeovers in neighbouring Mali, and cross-border security with Sierra Leone and Liberia. It works closely with the African Union and ECOWAS, and draws on its bauxite and mineral exports and partnerships with Senegal and Ivory Coast.

leader.name: Irfaan Ali
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Mohamed Irfaan Ali is a Guyanese politician serving as the tenth and current president of Guyana since 2020. A member of the People's Progressive Party/Civic, he previously served as the minister of Housing and Water from 2009 to 2015. He is the first Muslim to hold the office, and is the second Muslim head of state in the Americas after Noor Hassanali of Trinidad and Tobago. Head of government: Mark Phillips (Guyanese politician).

328.overview: Guyana's central geopolitical issue is its long-running territorial dispute with Venezuela over the Essequibo region, which Venezuela claims and which covers roughly two-thirds of Guyana's territory. The dispute has intensified since offshore oil discoveries, and Guyana relies on support from the United States, Brazil and its CARICOM partners to protect its sovereignty and offshore resources.

leader.name: Alix Didier Fils-Aimé
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Alix Didier Fils-Aimé is a Haitian businessman and politician who has served as the acting prime minister of Haiti since 2024, and became the country’s sole leader following the dissolution of the Transitional Presidential Council, starting on 7 February 2026. Head of state: Transitional Presidential Council.

332.overview: Haiti's central geopolitical concern is its internal breakdown rather than a territorial dispute: armed gangs control large parts of Port-au-Prince and much of the country's territory, and the state has struggled to govern. It shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, which maintains a tightly guarded border and is its most important neighbour. Haiti relies on the United States, regional bodies such as CARICOM and the OAS, and the international security mission backing its response to gang violence.

leader.name: Nasry Asfura
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Nasry Juan Asfura Zablah is a Honduran politician and construction businessman serving as the president of Honduras since 2026. A member of the National Party of Honduras, he previously served as the mayor of Tegucigalpa from 2014 to 2022.

340.overview: Honduras has no major territorial dispute or armed conflict with a neighbour, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its regional neighbours and outside influence. It shares borders with Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua, and works closely with these countries within the Organization of American States. Its most consequential external relationship is with the United States, which has a major influence on its security cooperation, migration flows and trade.

344.overview: Hong Kong has no independent geopolitical disputes of its own, as it is a Special Administrative Region of China under the "one country, two systems" framework. Its position is shaped by Beijing's authority over its foreign and defence affairs and by its role as a major financial and trade hub linking mainland China with global markets. Its international standing and economic ties are therefore closely tied to U.S.-China relations and to sanctions or trade measures affecting the mainland.

leader.name: Péter Magyar
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Péter Magyar is a Hungarian politician who has served as prime minister of Hungary since May 2026. He has been the president of the Tisza Party since 2024 and was a member of the European Parliament from 2024 to 2026. A former member of Fidesz, which governed Hungary from 2010 to 2026, Magyar rose to political prominence in 2024 in the wake of the Katalin Novák presidential pardon scandal. Head of state: Tamás Sulyok.

348.overview: Hungary has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its neighbours and its membership in Western institutions. Its relations with Slovakia, Serbia and Austria involve ethnic Hungarian minorities, and it relies on NATO and EU membership for security and trade. Russian gas supplies and energy dependence on Moscow also give Budapest significant leverage in its foreign policy.

leader.name: Kristrún Frostadóttir
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Kristrún Mjöll Frostadóttir is an Icelandic politician and economist who has served as the prime minister of Iceland since 2024, and leader of the Social Democratic Alliance since 2022. First elected to the Althing in the 2021 parliamentary election, she became Iceland's youngest-ever prime minister at the age of 36. As of March 2026, she is the world's second-youngest serving head of government behind Balen Shah. Head of state: Halla Tómasdóttir.

352.overview: Iceland has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its North Atlantic location and membership of NATO, on which it relies for collective defence despite having no standing army. It works closely with Norway, Denmark and the United Kingdom, and with the United States, which maintains a long defence relationship with the country. Fishing rights and Arctic shipping routes, as well as growing great-power interest in the High North, drive much of its foreign policy.

nuclear.range: Regional, extending toward intercontinental — Agni-V and SSBN fleet maturing.

leader.name: Narendra Modi
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Narendra Damodardas Modi is an Indian politician and statesman who has served as the prime minister of India since 26 May 2014. Modi was the chief minister of Gujarat from 2001 to 2014 and is the Member of Parliament for Varanasi. He is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party and of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, a right-wing Hindutva paramilitary volunteer organisation. Head of state: Droupadi Murmu.

356.overview: India's central geopolitical issue is its contested border with Pakistan, which both claim in full over Kashmir, with the two states having fought several wars and remaining armed rivals. India also faces an unresolved Himalayan border with China, where the two have clashed, and strategic competition with Beijing. It relies on partnerships with the United States, Japan, Australia and France through the Quad, and maintains traditional ties with Russia for defence and energy.

leader.name: Prabowo Subianto
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of the Republic of Indonesia.

360.overview: Indonesia's main geopolitical concerns are maritime rather than territorial: China's expansive nine-dash line overlaps the waters of the Natuna Islands, prompting Jakarta to assert its exclusive economic zone without formally recognising the claim. Indonesia has no active border conflicts and is not party to the South China Sea sovereignty disputes, positioning itself as a neutral mediator within ASEAN. It relies on Australia, Japan, the United States and Singapore for security and trade, and its position in the Malacca and Sunda Straits gives it major shipping leverage.

leader.name: Mojtaba Khamenei
leader.title: Supreme Leader
leader.bio: 3rd Supreme Leader of Iran since 2026. Head of government: Masoud Pezeshkian.

364.overview: Iran's central geopolitical issue is its rivalry with the United States and Israel, which view its nuclear programme and support for regional armed groups as threats, while Iran sees them as hostile powers. It contests influence across the Persian Gulf with Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, and its islands dispute with the UAE over Abu Musa and the Tunbs remains unresolved. Iran leans on Russia, China, Syria and Iraq, and uses its control of the Strait of Hormuz as major leverage over global oil flows.

leader.name: Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Prime Minister of Iraq from 2022 to 2026. Head of state: Nizar Amidi.

368.overview: Iraq's central geopolitical concern is its relationship with Iran, which exerts deep political and security influence through allied Shia militias, alongside a long-running dispute with Turkey over Turkish military operations and bases in northern Iraq. The Kurdistan Region's autonomy and contested areas such as Kirkuk remain sources of tension with Erbil and Baghdad. Iraq relies on the United States for security cooperation, and its oil exports through OPEC give it major economic leverage.

leader.name: Micheál Martin
leader.title: Taoiseach
leader.bio: Micheál Martin is an Irish Fianna Fáil politician serving as Taoiseach since January 2025, having previously held the position from 2020 to 2022. Martin served as Tánaiste, Minister for Foreign Affairs and Minister for Defence from December 2022 to January 2025. He has been leader of Fianna Fáil since January 2011 and a TD for Cork South-Central since 1989. Head of state: Catherine Connolly.

372.overview: Ireland's central geopolitical question is its relationship with the United Kingdom, shaped by the unresolved status of Northern Ireland and the border that runs across the island, which became a sensitive issue after Brexit. Its security is closely tied to the European Union and to NATO partners such as the United States, France and Germany, and it remains militarily neutral. Trade with the UK and the EU, and Atlantic shipping and energy links, shape its external position.

nuclear.range: Regional — undeclared arsenal, presumed air- and sea-delivered.

leader.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Prime Minister of Israel,. Head of state: Isaac Herzog.

376.overview: Israel's central geopolitical challenge is its conflict with Palestinians over the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem, where Israel occupies territory claimed by the Palestinians. It faces a hostile axis of Iran and its regional proxies, including Hezbollah in Lebanon, Houthi forces in Yemen, and Syria, with Iran's nuclear programme a core concern. Israel relies heavily on its security alliance with the United States, with further diplomatic and defence ties to Germany, the United Kingdom and several Arab states including the UAE, Bahrain and Morocco.

leader.name: Giorgia Meloni
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Giorgia Meloni is an Italian politician who has served as Prime Minister of Italy since October 2022. She is the first and only woman to hold the office and the head of the longest-serving government in the history of the Italian Republic. Head of state: Sergio Mattarella.

380.overview: Italy's longstanding geopolitical concerns are less about territorial disputes than about its position in the Mediterranean, where migration flows from North Africa and instability in Libya shape its security agenda. It relies on NATO, with US forces and nuclear weapons based at Aviano and Ghedi, and on the European Union for economic and migration policy. Its partnerships with France, Germany and Spain anchor its influence in Europe, and its exposure to Russian gas supply has driven diversification of energy sources.

leader.name: Alassane Ouattara
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Alassane Dramane Ouattara is an Ivorian politician and economist who has been President of Ivory Coast since 2010. An economist by profession, he worked for the International Monetary Fund and the Central Bank of West African States, and was the Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire from November 1990 to December 1993, appointed to that post by then-President Félix Houphouët-Boigny. Head of government: Robert Beugré Mambé.

384.overview: Côte d'Ivoire has no major territorial disputes or armed rivalries, so its position is shaped mainly by its neighbours and regional ties. Its 2010–2011 post-election crisis and cross-border militancy from the Sahel, especially along the Burkina Faso frontier, drive security cooperation. It relies on France for military and economic ties, works closely with Ghana and Senegal, and sits within ECOWAS and the African Union.

leader.name: Andrew Holness
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Andrew Michael Holness, MP is a Jamaican politician who has served as Prime Minister of Jamaica since 3 March 2016, having previously served from 2011 to 2012, and as leader of the Jamaica Labour Party since 2011. Holness previously served as prime minister from 23 October 2011 to 5 January 2012. Head of state: Charles III.

388.overview: Jamaica has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its Caribbean neighbourhood and close ties to outside powers. It relies on the United States and the United Kingdom for security cooperation and trade, and works within CARICOM and the Commonwealth. Its exposure to hurricanes, tourism dependence and migration flows through the region are its main external pressures.

leader.name: Sanae Takaichi
leader.title: Prime Minister
