leader.bio: Sanae Takaichi is a Japanese politician who has been Prime Minister of Japan and President of the Liberal Democratic Party since October 2025. She is the first woman to hold either of these positions in Japanese history. A member of the House of Representatives from 1993 to 2003 and since 2005, she also held ministerial posts during the premierships of Shinzo Abe and Fumio Kishida. Head of state: Naruhito.

392.overview: Japan's central security concern is China's assertiveness in the East China Sea, where both claim the Senkaku Islands (called Diaoyu in China) and Chinese maritime activity around them is persistent, alongside tensions over Taiwan. North Korean missile tests and an unresolved territorial dispute with Russia over the southern Kuril Islands add pressure. Japan relies heavily on its alliance with the United States and deepening ties with Australia, the Philippines and India.

leader.name: Kassym-Jomart Tokayev
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Kassym-Jomart Kemeluly Tokayev is a Kazakh politician and diplomat who has served as the second president of Kazakhstan since 2019. He previously served as Prime Minister from 1999 to 2002 and as Chairman of the Senate from 2007 to 2011 and again from 2013 to 2019. Tokayev also held the position of Director-General of the United Nations Office at Geneva from 2011 to 2013. Head of government: Oljas Bektenov.

398.overview: Kazakhstan's main geopolitical balancing act is its dependence on Russia, which shares its long northern border and historically dominates the region's security and transit routes, while it simultaneously cultivates China as a major investor and trade partner. Its border with Russia and the Caspian Sea boundary with neighbours such as Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan remain areas of careful management. Kazakhstan relies on Russian-controlled pipelines for much of its oil exports and on the CSTO and EAEU for security and economic ties, while maintaining wider diplomatic ties through the SCO and OIC.

leader.name: Jafar Hassan
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Jafar Hassan is a Jordanian politician who has served as the Prime Minister of Jordan since 2024. Hassan worked in Jordan's diplomatic service and was chief of staff for Abdullah II of Jordan. Head of state: Abdullah II.

400.overview: Jordan's position is shaped less by territorial disputes than by its neighbours and dependence on outside support. It borders Israel and the occupied West Bank, Syria and Iraq, and absorbs large refugee flows from Syria, Iraq and the Palestinian territories, while its security relies heavily on the United States and Gulf partners such as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. Limited energy resources and reliance on Gulf and Western aid leave it highly exposed to regional instability.

leader.name: William Ruto
leader.title: President
leader.bio: William Kipchirchir Samoei Arap Ruto is a Kenyan politician who is the fifth and current president of Kenya since 13 September 2022. Prior to becoming president, he served as the first elected deputy president of Kenya from 2013 to 2022. He previously served in three cabinet portfolios as the Minister for Home Affairs, the Minister of Agriculture and as Minister for Higher Education.

404.overview: Kenya's main external concern is the spillover of instability from its volatile neighbourhood, particularly the Al-Shabaab insurgency in Somalia and the Horn of Africa's recurring crises. Its long-running border tensions with Somalia over the Ilemi Triangle and maritime boundary issues remain points of friction. Kenya relies on regional partnerships through the East African Community and the African Union, and on Western security and aid ties with the United States and the United Kingdom.

nuclear.range: Regional, with a developing intercontinental-range capability.

leader.name: Kim Jong Un
leader.title: Supreme Leader
leader.bio: Kim Jong Un is a North Korean politician and dictator who has been serving as the supreme leader of North Korea since 2011, following the death of his father, Kim Jong Il. He is the third ruler from the Kim family to lead the country, which was founded by his grandfather Kim Il Sung. Head of government: Pak Thae-song.

408.overview: North Korea's central issue is the unresolved Korean War: it has no peace treaty with South Korea or the United States, and it maintains a heavily armed border and a nuclear arsenal that it treats as its main deterrent. Its primary adversaries are the United States, South Korea and Japan, and it has repeatedly threatened missile and nuclear escalation against them. It relies heavily on China, its main economic lifeline and diplomatic shield, and on Russia, which has deepened military and economic ties.

leader.name: Lee Jae Myung
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Lee Jae Myung is a South Korean politician and lawyer who has served as the 14th president of South Korea since 2025. A member of the Democratic Party of Korea, he was the party's leader while serving as member of the National Assembly for Incheon Gyeyang B from 2022 to 2025. Lee previously served as governor of Gyeonggi from 2018 to 2021 and as mayor of Seongnam from 2010 to 2018.

410.overview: South Korea's central security concern is North Korea, which it still technically remains at war with after the 1950–53 Korean War that ended in an armistice rather than a peace treaty. Pyongyang's nuclear and missile programs and its border provocations, including along the heavily fortified Demilitarized Zone, drive Seoul's defence posture. Seoul depends heavily on its military alliance with the United States, which stations troops on the peninsula, and maintains close security and trade ties with Japan and other partners.

leader.name: Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah
leader.title: Emir
leader.bio: Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah is Emir of Kuwait, reigning since 2023. Mishal spent most of his career in Kuwait's security and intelligence apparatus. Prior to becoming Emir at age 83, he was the oldest crown prince in the world. Head of government: Sabah Al-Khalid Al-Sabah.

414.overview: Kuwait's central concern is its northern border with Iraq, which Iraq disputed in 1961 and again in its 1990 invasion, when Kuwait was occupied until a US-led coalition expelled Iraqi forces. Its Gulf neighbours and Iran have also contested offshore oil fields and the Khor Abdullah waterway. Kuwait relies on its security partnership with the United States and on Saudi Arabia, while its oil output within OPEC gives it significant influence over global energy markets.

leader.name: Sadyr Japarov
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Kyrgyz politician and the president of Kyrgyzstan. Head of government: Adylbek Kasymaliev.

417.overview: Kyrgyzstan's most consequential issue is its unresolved border with Tajikistan, which has seen periodic deadly clashes over disputed enclaves and water access in the Fergana Valley. It also shares contested frontier sections with Uzbekistan. The country relies heavily on Russia for security through the CSTO and on Russian and Chinese economic ties, while Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan remain key regional partners.

leader.name: Thongloun Sisoulith
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Thongloun Sisoulith is a Laotian politician and historian who serves as the general secretary of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party and the seventh president of Laos since 2021. Thongloun was born and educated in Houaphanh province, before receiving education in Leningrad and Moscow in the Soviet Union. During the Laotian Civil War, he supported the Pathet Lao as a teacher. Head of government: Sonexay Siphandone.

418.overview: Laos has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts with its neighbours, and its position is shaped mainly by its close ties to Vietnam and China. China's rapidly expanding influence through infrastructure and lending, especially the China-Laos railway, is a major factor in its economy and foreign relations. Laos is landlocked and depends on Thailand and Vietnam for trade routes and seaports, and it relies on its ASEAN membership to balance these relationships.

leader.name: Nawaf Salam
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Lebanese Prime Minister. Head of state: Joseph Aoun.

422.overview: Lebanon's central geopolitical issue is its long-running conflict with Israel, including the unresolved land border, the Shebaa Farms area that Lebanon claims and Israel occupied, and the disputed maritime boundary in the eastern Mediterranean. Hezbollah, a powerful armed group in southern Lebanon, is viewed by Israel as its principal threat. Lebanon depends on France and Saudi Arabia for diplomatic and financial support, while Syria's influence over its politics and borders remains significant.

leader.name: Sam Matekane
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Ntsokoane Samuel Matekane is a Mosotho businessman and politician who is the current Prime Minister of Lesotho since 2022. Prior to running, he was considered to be the richest person in the country. Matekane made his fortune in diamond mining, as well as through government issued construction contracts. Head of state: Letsie III.

426.overview: Lesotho has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts with its neighbours, and its borders with South Africa are entirely landlocked and undisputed. Its position is shaped by its near-total encirclement by South Africa, on which it depends for trade, water, electricity and migrant labour, and by its membership in the Southern African Development Community and African Union. Political instability and periodic internal tensions are handled mainly through regional mediation, with South African involvement as a key partner.

leader.name: Andris Kulbergs
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Andris Kulbergs is a Latvian businessman and politician serving as the prime minister of Latvia since 2026. Before being elected to the Saeima as a non-party member of the United List ticket in 2022, he worked in a number of roles in the private sector. He also serves as the president of the Latvian Authorised Automobile Dealers Association. Head of state: Edgars Rinkēvičs.

428.overview: Latvia's central concern is its exposure to Russia, which it sees as a direct threat given their long border and Russia's ties to the Russian-speaking population and the Baltic region, with Belarus adding pressure on its eastern frontier. Latvia relies on NATO collective defence and a US military presence, alongside close cooperation with Lithuania, Estonia and Poland. It has no active armed conflict or territorial dispute with a neighbour.

leader.name: Joseph Boakai
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr. is a Liberian politician who has served as the 26th president of Liberia since 2024. He previously served as the 29th vice president of Liberia from 2006 to 2018, under President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf and as the minister of agriculture from 1983 to 1985.

430.overview: Liberia has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its neighbours and partners. It is closely tied to the United States, its historic backer, and works through the African Union, ECOWAS and Sierra Leone, Ivory Coast and Guinea on regional stability and cross-border security. Its main external dependence is on aid and trade with Western partners rather than on any rival power.

leader.name: Aguila Saleh Issa
leader.title: Chairman
leader.bio: Aguila Saleh Issa Gueider is a Libyan jurist and politician who served as the Speaker of the Libyan House of Representatives from 2014 to 2026. Head of government: Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh.

434.overview: Libya's central issue is the split between rival governments and armed factions in the east and west, which has left the country divided and its oil wealth contested. Turkey and Egypt back opposing sides, while the United Arab Emirates, Russia and others have also shaped the conflict. Libya holds Africa's largest proven oil reserves, and its production and export terminals give it considerable leverage within OPEC and with European buyers such as Italy.

leader.name: Brigitte Haas
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Brigitte Haas is a Liechtensteiner lawyer and politician who has served as the prime minister of Liechtenstein since 2025. She is the first woman to hold the office. Head of state: Hans-Adam II of Liechtenstein.

438.overview: Liechtenstein has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its small size and its location between Switzerland and Austria. It relies on Swiss customs and monetary arrangements, and on its membership in the European Economic Area for market access. Its security rests largely on those neighbours and on its own tiny army, which was disbanded in 1868.

leader.name: Mindaugas Sinkevičius
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Mindaugas Sinkevičius is a Lithuanian manager and politician, who has served as the 20th Prime Minister of Lithuania since 14 July 2026. He also served as Mayor of Jonava District Municipality, former Minister of Economy of Lithuania and Vice-Mayor of Jonava. Head of state: Gitanas Nausėda.

440.overview: Lithuania's central concern is Russia, which it views as a direct threat given the Kaliningrad exclave bordering it and the Russian-backed Belarusian regime to its east, with Russia's war in Ukraine heightening that risk. Lithuania relies on NATO collective defence, a substantial allied military presence, and close ties with the United States, Poland, Germany, Latvia, Estonia and Ukraine. It has no active territorial disputes of its own.

leader.name: Émile Reuter
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Émile Reuter was a Luxembourgish politician. He served as prime minister of Luxembourg for six years, from 28 June 1918 until 20 March 1925. Head of state: Guillaume V of Luxembourg.

442.overview: Luxembourg has no territorial disputes, rivalries or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped by its membership in the European Union and NATO and its close partnerships with Belgium, the Netherlands, France and Germany. As a small state bordering France, Germany and Belgium, it relies on EU single-market rules, shared security commitments and cooperation with its larger neighbours on trade, finance and defence.

446.overview: Macao is a Special Administrative Region of China and has no territorial disputes of its own; its political position is defined by its relationship with Beijing under the "one country, two systems" framework. Its economy depends heavily on gambling tourism from mainland China and Hong Kong, so Chinese policy and cross-border travel rules are its main external pressure. Portugal, which ruled the territory until 1999, retains cultural and legal ties but no governing role.

leader.name: Michael Randrianirina
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Malagasy military officer and president of Madagascar since 2025. Head of government: Mamitiana Rajaonarison.

450.overview: Madagascar has no active territorial dispute of major note, so its position is shaped by its Indian Ocean setting and external partners. It is a member of the African Union and the Southern African Development Community, and relies on France, its former colonial power, along with Mauritius and the Comoros for regional ties. Its contested waters and islands, including the Scattered Islands claimed by France, are a longstanding source of Indian Ocean maritime attention.

leader.name: Peter Mutharika
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Arthur Peter Mutharika is a Malawian politician and lawyer who has been the seventh president of Malawi since 2025. A member of the Democratic Progressive Party and the younger brother of the third president, Bingu wa Mutharika, he served as the fifth president from 2014 to 2020 and has also been leading the DPP since 2012. Head of government: Lazarus Chakwera.

454.overview: Malawi has no major territorial disputes or active armed rivalries, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its landlocked location and regional ties. It depends on neighbouring Mozambique and Tanzania for access to Indian Ocean ports and on Zambia for transport links, while its place in the African Union and the Southern African Development Community anchors its diplomacy. Aid partnerships and migration pressures across the region also weigh heavily on its policy choices.

leader.name: Anwar Ibrahim
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Anwar bin Ibrahim is a Malaysian politician who has served as the 10th prime minister of Malaysia since 2022. A member of the People's Justice Party, he served as Member of Parliament for Tambun since 2022. Upon becoming prime minister, he appointed himself Minister of Finance. Head of state: Ibrahim Iskandar of Johor.

458.overview: Malaysia's main geopolitical concern is the South China Sea, where it contests parts of the Spratly Islands and maritime waters claimed by China, alongside Vietnam, the Philippines, Brunei and Taiwan. Its strategic position on the Strait of Malacca, one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, shapes its trade and security ties. Malaysia engages with Singapore, Indonesia and Thailand through ASEAN and balances close economic relations with China against defence and diplomatic links to other regional powers.

leader.name: Mohamed Muizzu
leader.title: President
leader.bio: 8th President of the Maldives since 2023.

462.overview: The Maldives has no major territorial dispute or armed conflict, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its vulnerability as a low-lying island state. Climate change and rising sea levels are its most serious long-term threat. It relies heavily on India for security and economic support, while its position on Indian Ocean shipping lanes draws influence from China and other major powers.

leader.name: Assimi Goita
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Assimi Goita is a Malian politician and military officer who has ruled Mali since 2021. He has served as the sixth president of Mali since 2025, previously serving as the interim vice president under Interim President Bah Ndaw from 2020 to 2021 and then as the interim president until 2025. He also served as the president of the Alliance of Sahel States from 2024 to 2025. Head of government: Abdoulaye Maiga (officer).

466.overview: Mali's central geopolitical issue is the insurgency in its north, where jihadist and Tuareg separatist groups have contested control of the Sahara and the border areas with Algeria, which Mali accuses of backing rebels. Its military government relies heavily on Russia for security support and on fellow Sahel juntas Burkina Faso and Niger through the Alliance of Sahel States, while tensions with Algeria remain sharp.

leader.name: Robert Abela
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Robert Abela is a Maltese lawyer and politician who has served as prime minister of Malta and leader of the Malta Labour Party since 2020, following the resignation of Joseph Muscat on 13 January that year. The son of former president George Abela, he was elected to Parliament in 2017. Head of state: Myriam Spiteri Debono.

470.overview: Malta's main geopolitical concerns are its position in the central Mediterranean, where it faces migration pressure from North Africa and must coordinate with Italy and the European Union on search-and-rescue and border responsibilities. It has no territorial disputes with neighbours, and its security rests on EU membership, its partnership with Italy, and ties with the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth.

leader.name: Mohamed Ould Ghazouani
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Mohamed Ould Cheikh Mohamed Ahmed Ould Ghazouani, also known as Ghazouani and Ould Ghazouani, is a Mauritanian politician and retired army general who has been the 9th President of Mauritania since 2019, and the 22nd chairperson of the African Union from February 2024 until February 2025. Ghazouani is a former general-director of National Security and former chief of staff of the Armed Forces of Mauritania. Head of government: Mokhtar Ould Djay.

478.overview: Mauritania's position is shaped less by border disputes than by its western Sahara neighbourhood, where Morocco's claim and control over Western Sahara and the Polisario Front's independence push have made the region unsettled and drawn Mauritania into regional balancing. Its border with Mali and recurring jihadist activity in the Sahel add security pressure, while it relies on Senegal, Morocco and Algeria for regional diplomacy, and on European and African Union partners for security and migration cooperation.

leader.name: Dharam Gokhool
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Dharambeer Gokhool is a Mauritian politician who has been serving as the president of Mauritius since 6 December 2024. He won the 2024 presidential election with the backing of the Labour Party. Head of government: Pravind Jugnauth.

480.overview: Mauritius's main long-standing issue is its sovereignty dispute with the United Kingdom over the Chagos Archipelago, including Diego Garcia, which Mauritius claims and which the UK administers as the British Indian Ocean Territory. The dispute is pursued through international legal channels and has drawn in India, Madagascar and the African Union, which support Mauritius's position. Its diplomacy is shaped by close ties with India and France and membership in the Commonwealth and SADC.

leader.name: Claudia Sheinbaum
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo is a Mexican politician, energy and climate change scientist, and academic who has been serving as the 66th president of Mexico since 2024. She is the first woman and the first person of Jewish heritage to hold the office. A member of the National Regeneration Movement, she previously served as Head of Government of Mexico City from 2018 to 2023.

484.overview: Mexico's geopolitical position is shaped less by territorial disputes than by its relationship with the United States, its northern neighbour and principal trade partner, where migration, drug trafficking, and cross-border security cooperation dominate policy. Mexico has no active border disputes or armed conflicts, and its regional standing rests on a shared border of over 3,000 kilometres, economic integration through USMCA, and oil and energy leverage. Ties with Canada, Spain, and Colombia, along with multilateral membership in the OAS and G20, anchor its diplomacy.

leader.name: Christophe Mirmand
leader.title: Minister
leader.bio: Christophe Jacques-Pierre Mirmand is a French government official who was appointed the 26th minister of state of Monaco under Prince Albert II on 21 July 2025. He succeeded Isabelle Berro-Amadeï, who held the office in an acting capacity following the death of Didier Guillaume. Head of state: Albert II of Monaco.

492.overview: Monaco has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its security rests on its own small size and its treaty relationship with France, which guarantees its independence and handles much of its defence. Its main external pressures are economic and regulatory, shaped by France and the European Union, particularly over tax transparency and banking rules. Its border with France is uncontested, and it is a close partner of its larger neighbour rather than a rival to any power.

leader.name: Nyam-Osoryn Uchral
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Nyam-Osoryn Uchral is a Mongolian politician, businessman and former hip-hop artist who has been the Prime Minister of Mongolia since 30 March 2026 and the Chairman of the Mongolian People's Party since 15 November 2025. A member of the Mongolian People's Party, he was elected a member of the State Great Khural in 2016, 2020, and 2024. Head of state: Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh.

496.overview: Mongolia has no major territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its position is shaped by its position between Russia and China, the two powers on its borders. It relies on both for trade, since its landlocked economy depends on their rail and road routes to the sea, and it cultivates third-neighbour ties with Japan, South Korea and the United States to balance their influence.

leader.name: Maia Sandu
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Maia Sandu is a Moldovan politician and economist who, since 2020, has served as the sixth president of Moldova. She is the founder and former leader of the Party of Action and Solidarity and was prime minister of Moldova from June to November 2019, when her government collapsed after a vote of no-confidence. Head of government: Vasile Tofan.

498.overview: Moldova's central issue is the breakaway region of Transnistria, a Russian-backed enclave on its eastern bank of the Dniester where Russian troops remain stationed without consent from Chisinau. Moldova also faces Russian pressure over its European integration and its ties to Romania and Ukraine. Its ties to the European Union, Romania, France and the United States are central to its security and economy, while Russia remains its main adversary.

leader.name: Milojko Spajić
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Milojko Spajić is a Montenegrin politician serving as Prime Minister of Montenegro since October 2023. He previously served as minister of finance and social welfare in the Krivokapić Cabinet from 2020 to 2022. He is also the leader and co-founder of the Europe Now! Head of state: Jakov Milatović.

499.overview: Montenegro's central geopolitical concern is its relationship with Serbia, where questions over the Montenegrin Orthodox Church, national identity and the 2006 state's borders remain politically sensitive, though not an active dispute. Its border with Albania, including the Ulcinj coast and Lake Skadar, has been settled through agreements, leaving few open claims. Montenegro relies on its NATO membership, joined in 2017, and close ties with the United States, while its Adriatic coast and tourism-driven economy make it sensitive to regional stability and Russian and Chinese investment.

leader.name: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri is a Moroccan politician and lawyer who is the prime minister of Morocco since 29 September 2026. She is the first woman to hold the office. A member of the Authenticity and Modernity Party, she previously served as mayor of Marrakesh, first from 2009 to 2015, and then since 2021. Head of state: Mohammed VI of Morocco.

504.overview: Morocco's central dispute is its claim to Western Sahara, a territory it controls in most of its area while Algeria backs the Polisario Front, which seeks an independent state there. The two countries also have a rivalry over regional influence, and their border has been closed since 1994. Morocco relies on Spain, France and the United States, and on its own phosphate exports for leverage.

leader.name: Daniel Chapo
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Daniel Francisco Chapo is a Mozambican politician, lawyer and jurist who has been the president of Mozambique since 15 January 2025. Chapo previously served as the governor of Inhambane Province from 2016 to 2024. Chapo was the Secretary-General and candidate of the ruling political party, FRELIMO, for the 2024 presidential election. Head of government: Maria Benvinda Levy.

508.overview: Mozambique's most pressing concern is the insurgency in its northern Cabo Delgado province, where Islamist militants have fought government forces and disrupted the region's large offshore natural gas projects. Its relations with neighbours are shaped by border security and trade routes, and it relies on South Africa, Zimbabwe, Malawi and Tanzania for regional stability. Support from Rwanda and Southern African Development Community partners has helped contain the fighting, while the gas sector draws in foreign investors.

leader.name: Haitham bin Tariq
leader.title: Sultan
leader.bio: Haitham bin Tariq Al Said is Sultan and Prime Minister of Oman. He acceded to the throne in 2020 following the death of his cousin, Sultan Qaboos bin Said, becoming the fifteenth ruler of the Al Bu Said dynasty, which has ruled Oman since the mid-eighteenth century. Haitham was born in Muscat to Sayyid Tariq bin Taimur, an uncle of Sultan Qaboos who served as his first Prime Minister from 1970 to 1972.

512.overview: Oman's position is shaped less by territorial disputes than by its location on the Strait of Hormuz, through which a large share of the world's seaborne oil passes, and by its careful balancing between Iran across the strait and its Gulf Arab neighbours. Oman maintains close ties with Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom, and is a member of the Gulf Cooperation Council, the Arab League and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation. It has often served as a mediator, maintaining channels to Tehran that its neighbours do not.

leader.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Ndemupelila Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, nicknamed NNN, is a Namibian politician who is the fifth and current president of Namibia since 21 March 2025. She is the country's first female president. Previously, she served as the third vice president under President Nangolo Mbumba between 2024 and 2025. Head of government: Elijah Ngurare.

516.overview: Namibia has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its position is shaped by its neighbours and partners rather than by rivalry. Its closest ties run to South Africa, Botswana and Angola, with the Southern African Development Community as its main regional framework. Its economy depends heavily on diamonds and uranium, and its foreign policy is shaped by African Union and Commonwealth membership.

leader.name: David Adeang
leader.title: President
leader.bio: David Ranibok Waiau Adeang is a Nauruan politician, currently serving as President of Nauru. Adeang is the former Speaker of the Parliament of Nauru, and Nauru's Minister of Finance and Justice, as well as the Minister Assisting the President of Nauru.

520.overview: Nauru's main geopolitical concerns are existential rather than territorial: as a very low-lying island state it faces rising sea levels and climate risk that threaten its habitability. It has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and it relies on Australia for aid, security and a major role in regional migration processing. Its position is shaped by its membership in the Pacific Islands Forum and the Commonwealth, and by competing diplomatic influence from China and Taiwan, which it has switched recognition between.

leader.name: Pushpa Kamal Dahal
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Pushpa Kamal Dahal, popularly known as Prachanda, is a Nepalese politician. He is a member of House of Representatives elected from Eastern Rukum. He has been the prime minister of Nepal for three terms: from 2008 to 2009, from 2016 to 2017, and again from December 2022 until July 2024. Head of state: Ram Chandra Paudel.

524.overview: Nepal's central geopolitical position is shaped by its landlocked location between India and China, with a long-standing unresolved boundary dispute with India over Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura in the Kali River area. Nepal relies heavily on India for trade transit, fuel and imports, while China is a growing economic partner through Himalayan infrastructure and aid. It also balances between these two powers, with Bangladesh and others as secondary partners.

leader.name: Rob Jetten
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Prime minister of the Netherlands. Head of state: Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands.

528.overview: The Netherlands has no territorial disputes or active security rivalries, so its position is shaped mainly by its European and transatlantic commitments. It is a NATO and EU member, hosts US nuclear weapons under NATO nuclear sharing, and works closely with Germany, Belgium and the United Kingdom. Its major port of Rotterdam and maritime trade links give it substantial economic leverage within Europe.

531.overview: Curaçao's geopolitical position is shaped less by territorial disputes than by its status within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, which handles its defence and foreign affairs. It has no contested borders or armed rivalries, and its main external ties are with the Netherlands, the wider Caribbean, and the United States, whose influence and regional security role matter for its economy and stability. Its small size and reliance on trade, tourism and migration from neighbouring Venezuela are the factors that most affect its position.

533.overview: Aruba is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands and has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts. Its geopolitical position is shaped by its Caribbean neighbours, especially Venezuela, whose political and economic crisis has driven migration and smuggling through regional waters. Its ties to the Netherlands and the wider Kingdom, along with tourism-dependent trade with the United States, define its external relationships.

534.overview: Sint Maarten, the southern half of the island of Saint Martin, shares its landmass with the French collectivity of Saint-Martin to the north, and the two have no contested border between them. Its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its status as a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, which handles its defence and foreign affairs, and by its exposure to Caribbean hurricanes and regional migration flows. Tourism and cruise traffic are its key economic links, with the United States and the Netherlands as its main external ties.

540.overview: New Caledonia's central political question is its future status within France, after three referendums on independence (2018, 2020, 2021) rejected separation in narrow votes, with Kanak independence movements such as FLNKS still pressing for sovereignty. The territory's nickel reserves, among the world's largest, give it major economic leverage, and it relies heavily on France for budgetary support, security and governance. Its Pacific neighbours, Australia and Vanuatu, and rivalry among larger powers over Pacific influence, especially China, also shape its strategic position.

leader.name: Bob Loughman
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Bob Loughman Weibur is a Vanuatuan politician who served as Prime Minister of the Republic of Vanuatu between April 2020 and November 2022. Head of state: Nikenike Vurobaravu.

548.overview: Vanuatu has no major territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its vulnerability as a small Pacific island state exposed to climate change and rising sea levels. It relies on Australia, New Zealand and France, the former colonial power, for security cooperation, aid and development finance. Its membership in the Commonwealth and the Pacific Islands Forum gives it a voice in regional affairs, while growing Chinese and other great-power engagement in the Pacific draws attention to its strategic location.

leader.name: Christopher Luxon
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Christopher Mark Luxon is a New Zealand politician and businessman who has served as the 42nd prime minister of New Zealand since 2023. A member of the National Party, he has been the member of Parliament for Botany since 2020 and previously served as leader of the Opposition from 2021 to 2023. Prior to entering politics, he was the chief executive officer of Air New Zealand from 2013 to 2019. Head of state: Charles III.

554.overview: New Zealand has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its Pacific neighbourhood and its alliances. Its security ties run through the Five Eyes intelligence partnership with Australia, the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada, and it is a major non-NATO ally of the United States. Regional concerns centre on climate vulnerability and development across the Pacific Islands Forum, and on strategic competition in the Pacific, particularly China's growing influence.

leader.name: Daniel Ortega
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of Nicaragua.

558.overview: Nicaragua's most significant geopolitical friction is with the United States, which has sharply criticised its government and imposed sanctions over democratic backsliding, shaping its external position. Managua leans on Venezuela, Cuba and Russia for political and economic backing, and it maintains ties with Honduras across their shared border. As an OAS member, Nicaragua faces regional pressure over governance, while migration flows and climate vulnerability further influence its relations with neighbours.

leader.name: Hassoumi Massaoudou
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Hassoumi Massaoudou is a Nigerien politician who served as minister of Foreign Affairs of Niger from 2021 to 2023 and as minister of Finance from October 2016 to January 2019. Head of government: Ali Lamine Zeine.

562.overview: Niger's central geopolitical challenge is insurgency and cross-border militancy in the Sahel, with jihadist groups active along its frontiers with Mali and Burkina Faso and in the Lake Chad and Tillabéri areas. Its border with Benin and Nigeria, and the arid northern desert, remain difficult to police. Niger leans on its partners in the Alliance of Sahel States, notably Mali and Burkina Faso, on Chad, and on Russia for security cooperation, while its uranium resources have made it a focus of outside interest.

leader.name: Bola Tinubu
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Adekunle Tinubu is a Nigerian politician serving as the 16th and current president of Nigeria since 2023. He previously served as the governor of Lagos State from 1999 to 2007 and senator for Lagos West in the Third Republic. Tinubu spent his early life in southwestern Nigeria and later moved to the United States where he studied accounting at Chicago State University.

566.overview: Nigeria's most pressing concerns are internal: insurgency by Boko Haram and ISWAP in the northeast, banditry and kidnapping in the northwest, and farmer-herder violence in the Middle Belt. Its border security is strained by the Sahel, where jihadist groups operate across Niger, Cameroon and Benin. Nigeria relies on regional bodies such as ECOWAS and the African Union for diplomatic weight, and on US and UK security and counterterrorism cooperation. Its oil exports underpin its economy and give it influence within OPEC.

leader.name: Jonas Gahr Støre
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Jonas Gahr Støre is a Norwegian politician who has served as the prime minister of Norway since 2021. He has been leader of the Labour Party since 2014. He served under prime minister Jens Stoltenberg as minister of foreign affairs from 2005 to 2012 and as minister of health and care services from 2012 to 2013. Head of state: Haakon VIII.

578.overview: Norway's central geopolitical concern is its relationship with Russia, its neighbour along the Arctic and northern border and a long-standing adversary, where tensions over Svalbard, the High North and Barents Sea resources persist. Norway's security rests on its NATO membership and close ties with the United States, the United Kingdom and fellow Nordic states Sweden, Denmark, Finland and Iceland. As a major oil and gas exporter, its energy leverage gives it influence in European markets.

580.overview: The Northern Mariana Islands is a self-governing commonwealth of the United States, and its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by that tie rather than by any territorial dispute. Its main external concerns are its exposure to typhoons and sea-level rise across the western Pacific, the influence of Guam and US defence planning in the region, and its reliance on US federal funding, citizenship rights and immigration rules. It has no contested borders or armed conflicts.

leader.name: Wesley Simina
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Wesley Simina is a Micronesian politician who has been the 10th President of the Federated States of Micronesia since 2023. Prior to his presidency he was Speaker of the Congress of the Federated States of Micronesia from 2015 to 2023, a member of Congress from 2011 to 2023, and Governor of Chuuk from 2005 to 2011. He was a lawyer active in Chuuk prior to his political career.

583.overview: Micronesia's geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its relationship with the United States, which it relies on under a Compact of Free Association for defence, financial support and access to US services. Its key external concerns are the vulnerability of its low-lying islands to climate change and rising sea levels, and sustaining its fisheries in the Pacific Ocean, where it works through the Pacific Islands Forum. It has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts.

leader.name: Hilda Heine
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Hilda Cathy Heine is a Marshallese educator and politician. She has served as the president of the Marshall Islands since 2024, having previously served from 2016 to 2020. Heine was the first woman to lead any sovereign country in Micronesia and the first person from the Marshall Islands to earn a doctorate.

584.overview: The Marshall Islands' main geopolitical concerns are its vulnerability to rising sea levels and climate change, which threaten its low-lying atolls and the viability of its territory. It depends heavily on its Compact of Free Association with the United States, which provides defence responsibility, economic aid and rights to the Kwajalein missile test range. Regional ties through the Pacific Islands Forum, and growing Chinese diplomatic and economic influence in the Pacific, shape its foreign policy choices.

leader.name: Surangel Whipps Jr.
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Surangel Samuel Whipps Jr. is a Palauan businessman and politician who has served as the president of Palau since 2021. He previously served as a senator from 2009 to 2016.

585.overview: Palau's geopolitical position is shaped less by territorial disputes than by its strategic location and dependence on outside partners. Its exclusive economic zone lies in a sensitive part of the western Pacific, and it maintains a Compact of Free Association with the United States, which provides defence responsibility and substantial economic assistance. Its most significant external relationship is with Taiwan, one of its few diplomatic partners, which sits alongside growing Chinese pressure and competition for influence in the Pacific.

nuclear.range: Regional — short- to medium-range ballistic and cruise missiles.

leader.name: Shehbaz Sharif
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Prime Minister of Pakistan. Head of state: Asif Ali Zardari.

586.overview: Pakistan's central issue is Kashmir, which both Pakistan and India claim in full and which has been a source of repeated armed conflict between them. Its western border with Afghanistan is also contested and militarily tense, and it faces cross-border militancy from groups operating out of Afghan territory. Pakistan relies on China for diplomatic cover, arms and infrastructure investment, and on Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Qatar and the UAE for financial support and partnership.

leader.name: José Raúl Mulino
leader.title: President
leader.bio: 39th President of Panama.

591.overview: Panama's main geopolitical weight comes from the Panama Canal, a vital trade route that the United States has long sought to keep secure and neutral, and whose management and security remain a sensitive bilateral issue. Panama has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours. Its position is shaped by its close relationship with Washington, its ties to Colombia and Costa Rica, and migration flows through the Darién Gap.

leader.name: James Marape
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: James Marape is a Papua New Guinean politician who has served as the prime minister of Papua New Guinea since May 2019. He has been a member of the National Parliament of Papua New Guinea since July 2007, representing the electorate of Tari-Pori Open in Hela Province in the New Guinea Highlands. He has held Cabinet Posts as Minister of Education, Minister of Finance, and Minister of Foreign Affairs. Head of state: Charles III.

598.overview: Papua New Guinea's main external concerns are not territorial but shaped by its neighbours and partners. Its position rests on close security and aid ties with Australia and New Zealand and a long border with Indonesia, where the Indonesian-controlled western half of New Guinea is a sensitive issue. It is a Commonwealth and Pacific Islands Forum member, and growing Chinese and US influence in the Pacific is a background factor in its diplomacy.

leader.name: Santiago Peña
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Santiago Peña Palacios is a Paraguayan politician and economist who has served as the 52nd president of Paraguay since 2023. Peña served on leadership boards for the Central Bank of Paraguay and Banco Amambay. He taught economics at the Catholic University of Asunción, and has published research papers on monetary policy and finance.

600.overview: Paraguay has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its longstanding concerns are mostly regional. Its position is shaped by its landlocked status, which relies on river access through Argentina and Brazil, and by the Itaipu and Yacyretá hydroelectric dams it shares with Brazil and Argentina. Its border regions with Brazil and Bolivia are a focus for smuggling and organised crime, and it works closely with its Mercosur and OAS partners.

leader.name: Keiko Fujimori
leader.title: President
leader.bio: 67th President of Peru.

604.overview: Peru's most significant longstanding issue is its border with Ecuador, which was disputed for much of the 20th century and largely settled by a 1998 peace agreement, with the frontier fully demarcated afterward. Peru has no active armed conflicts, and its main security concerns are internal, centred on drug trafficking and insurgent remnants in the Andean valleys. It relies on regional partnerships with Colombia, Chile, Ecuador and Brazil and works through the Organization of American States, while the Pacific coast gives it substantial trade and fishing leverage.

leader.name: Bongbong Marcos
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Ferdinand "Bongbong" Romualdez Marcos Jr., commonly referred to by the initials BBM or PBBM, is a Filipino politician who has served as the 17th president of the Philippines since 2022. He is the second child and only son of 10th president Ferdinand Marcos and former first lady Imelda Marcos.

608.overview: China and the Philippines both claim parts of the South China Sea, most notably the Spratly Islands and Scarborough Shoal, making maritime control the central flashpoint. Manila also disputes Chinese activity around Second Thomas Shoal, and Vietnam and Malaysia have overlapping claims in the same waters. The Philippines relies on its defence alliance with the United States and closer security ties with Japan, Australia and others, while the Luzon Strait and key sea lanes carry strategic weight.

leader.name: Donald Tusk
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Donald Franciszek Tusk is a Polish politician and historian who has served as the prime minister of Poland since 2023, previously holding the office from 2007 to 2014. Tusk was President of the European Council from 2014 to 2019 and led the European People's Party from 2019 to 2022. Head of state: Karol Nawrocki.

616.overview: Poland's central concern is Russia, which it views as its primary security threat, especially after Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, with Belarus acting as a close Russian partner along its eastern border. Poland hosts NATO forces and depends on the alliance and the United States for deterrence, while its support for Ukraine and its Baltic neighbours, Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, shapes its regional role. Germany and the European Union are key partners on trade and security.

leader.name: Luís Montenegro
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Luís Filipe Montenegro Cardoso de Morais Esteves is a Portuguese politician and lawyer serving as the prime minister of Portugal since April 2024, currently leading the 25th Constitutional Government. Additionally, he has been president of the Social Democratic Party since 2022. Head of state: António José Seguro.

620.overview: Portugal has no active territorial disputes or armed rivalries, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its Atlantic location and alliances. It is a NATO member and a European Union state, anchored by its partnership with Spain on the Iberian Peninsula. Its historic ties to Brazil, Angola and Mozambique, along with its bilateral relationship with the United States, shape its diplomacy, while migration flows and Atlantic security remain its main external concerns.

leader.name: Rui Duarte de Barros
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Rui Duarte de Barros is a Bissau-Guinean economist and politician who has served as the prime minister of Guinea-Bissau from 17 January 2024 to 7 August 2025. His previous positions include being the Minister of Economy and Finance, as well as being the acting prime minister from 16 May 2012 to 3 July 2014 following a military coup.

624.overview: Guinea-Bissau's main geopolitical exposure is internal instability, with recurring coups and power struggles between civilian leaders and the military that have repeatedly disrupted governance. It has no major territorial dispute with neighbours, though its maritime boundary with Senegal and the Casamance region's separatist legacy shape its relations. Regional stability is anchored by the African Union and ECOWAS, while Portugal, Senegal and Gambia remain key partners, with aid and drug-trafficking transit across its coast drawing outside attention.

leader.name: Xanana Gusmão
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: José Alexandre "Xanana" Gusmão is an East Timorese politician. He has served as the tenth prime minister of Timor-Leste since 2023, previously serving as the sixth prime minister from 2007 to 2015. A former rebel, he also served as East Timor's first president since its re-establishment of independence from 2002 to 2007. Head of state: José Ramos-Horta.

626.overview: Timor-Leste's main geopolitical concerns are its maritime boundaries with Australia, which were settled through negotiations over the Timor Sea's oil and gas fields, and its long-running reliance on Indonesia, which occupied the territory until 1999 and shares its land border. The Greater Sunrise gas field remains a point of tension over revenue sharing with Australia. Its position is shaped by ties to Australia, Indonesia and Portugal, and by ASEAN membership.

630.overview: Puerto Rico's status is its defining political question: it is a U.S. unincorporated territory whose residents are U.S. citizens but cannot vote for president and have no voting representation in Congress, and debate over statehood, independence and continued territorial status remains unresolved. Its security and defence are handled through the United States, and its economy depends heavily on U.S. federal funding, trade, shipping and the dollar. Hurricane vulnerability and debt pressures also shape its relationship with Washington.

leader.name: Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani
leader.title: Emir
leader.bio: Emir of Qatar since 2013. Head of government: Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani.

634.overview: Qatar has no major territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its neighbours and its energy wealth. Its long-running sensitivity has centred on the Gulf rivalry with Saudi Arabia and the UAE, which led to a blockade from 2017 to 2021. Qatar relies on its partnership with the United States, which hosts Al Udeid Air Base, and on ties with Turkey, while its vast gas reserves in the shared North Field give it significant leverage.

leader.name: Nicușor Dan
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Nicușor Daniel Dan is a Romanian mathematician and politician serving as the seventh President of Romania since 2025. He previously served as the Mayor of Bucharest from 2020 to 2025 and as a member of the Chamber of Deputies from 2016 to 2020. Head of government: Ilie Bolojan.

642.overview: Romania's central geopolitical concern is Russia's war in neighbouring Ukraine, which has placed Romania on NATO's eastern flank next to the Black Sea. Its longstanding frictions are mainly with Ukraine, over the Danube Delta and maritime boundaries in the Black Sea. Romania relies on NATO, its EU membership and its security partnership with the United States, and it hosts allied forces at Deveselu and Mihail Kogălniceanu.

leader.name: Vladimir Putin
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin is a Russian politician and former intelligence officer who has served as President of Russia since 2012, having previously served from 2000 to 2008. Putin also served as Prime Minister of Russia from 1999 to 2000 and again from 2008 to 2012. He has been described as the de facto leader of Russia since 1999. Head of government: Mikhail Mishustin.

643.overview: Russia's central geopolitical issue is its war with Ukraine, which includes Russian-occupied territory in eastern and southern Ukraine and a frozen-to-active confrontation with NATO over European security. Moscow is in deep rivalry with the United States and European states, while relying on China, Iran, North Korea and Belarus for diplomatic, economic and military backing. Its leverage rests heavily on oil and gas exports and its nuclear arsenal, with the CSTO, CIS and EAEU anchoring influence across former Soviet space.

leader.name: Paul Kagame
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of Rwanda since 2000. Head of government: Justin Nsengiyumva.

646.overview: Rwanda's central geopolitical issue is its strained relationship with the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which accuses Kigali of backing armed groups in eastern DR Congo, a charge Rwanda rejects while pointing to Congolese rebels, including remnants of groups linked to the 1994 genocide, operating across the border. Rwanda relies on its ties with Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania within the East African Community, and on backing from the United States, Commonwealth partners and the African Union, while aid dependence and regional mineral supply chains, notably tin, tantalum and tungsten, shape its external standing.

leader.name: Terrance Drew
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Terrance Michael Drew is a Kittitian medical doctor and politician who has served as the fourth and current prime minister of Saint Kitts and Nevis since 2022, and as leader of the Labour Party since 2021. Head of state: Charles III.

659.overview: Saint Kitts and Nevis has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its small size and dependence on partners. It relies on its membership in the Organization of American States, the Commonwealth and CARICOM for diplomatic backing and trade access. Its vulnerability to hurricanes, economic shocks and reliance on tourism and citizenship-by-investment programs shapes its foreign policy priorities.

leader.name: Philip J. Pierre
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Philip Joseph Pierre is a Saint Lucian politician currently serving as the prime minister of Saint Lucia since 2021. Pierre serves as the Minister for Finance, Economic Development and the Youth Economy. He is the Leader of the Saint Lucia Labour Party since 18 June 2016. Head of state: Charles III.

662.overview: Saint Lucia has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its small size and its dependence on partners. Its security and economic ties run through the Caribbean community, especially CARICOM and the OAS, alongside Commonwealth membership. Its vulnerability to hurricanes, rising sea levels and the loss of banana and tourism revenue is a more pressing concern than any rival state.

663.overview: Saint Martin is a small Caribbean island shared between France and the Netherlands, and its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by that split rather than by a territorial dispute. The French side is an overseas collectivity of France and the Dutch side is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, with the border between them open and unfenced. Its main external pressures are hurricanes, migration flows from neighbouring islands, and its reliance on France, the Netherlands and the European Union for security, aid and reconstruction.

leader.name: Godwin Friday
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Godwin Elliot Loraine Friday is a Vincentian politician who has served as Prime Minister of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines since 2025 and as leader of the New Democratic Party since 2016. He has been the Member of Parliament for the Northern Grenadines constituency since 2001 and served as the leader of the opposition from 2016 to 2025. Head of state: Charles III.

670.overview: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines has no major territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its small size and dependence on regional partners. It is a member of the Organization of American States, the Commonwealth and CARICOM, and relies on these bodies for trade, diplomatic backing and development support. Its exposure to hurricanes, climate pressures and the influence of larger regional powers in the Caribbean also shapes its foreign policy.

leader.name: Maria Luisa Berti
leader.title: Captain Regent
leader.bio: Captain Regent of San Marino.

674.overview: San Marino has no territorial disputes or armed rivalries, and its position is shaped mainly by its geography as a small enclave wholly surrounded by Italy. Its key relationship is with Italy, on which it depends for customs arrangements, currency and much of its trade and services. As a microstate it relies on international diplomacy and membership in multilateral bodies rather than military alliances or resource leverage.

leader.name: Carlos Vila Nova
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Carlos Manuel Vila Nova is a Santomean politician who is the fifth and current president of São Tomé and Príncipe, since 2 October 2021. He served as the Minister of Public Works and Natural Resources and minister of Infrastructure, Natural Resources and the Environment in successive governments of Prime Minister Patrice Trovoada. Head of government: Américo Ramos.

678.overview: São Tomé and Príncipe has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its position is shaped by its small size and reliance on outside partners. It depends heavily on Portugal for aid, governance support and cultural ties, and maintains close relations with Angola, its larger neighbour across the Gulf of Guinea. As a member of the African Union and other regional bodies, it looks to collective diplomacy for security and economic support.

leader.name: Salman of Saudi Arabia
leader.title: King
leader.bio: King of Saudi Arabia since 2015.

682.overview: Saudi Arabia's central security concern is its rivalry with Iran, which backs armed groups across the region, including in Yemen, where Saudi forces have fought Houthi rebels on its southern border. Riyadh also contests influence in Lebanon, Syria and Iraq with Tehran. It relies heavily on its security alliance with the United States, and on its oil export leverage through OPEC and the Strait of Hormuz.

leader.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, also known mononymously as Diomaye, is a Senegalese politician and former tax official who is serving as the fifth and current president of Senegal since 2024. He was previously the general secretary of PASTEF, and won the 2024 Senegalese presidential election in place of disqualified candidate Ousmane Sonko, whom he later appointed as prime minister.

686.overview: Senegal has no major territorial disputes or armed rivalries, so its position is shaped mainly by its neighbours and partners. Its southern border with Guinea-Bissau and the Casamance region, where a long separatist insurgency has largely wound down, remain sensitive. Senegal leans on France, its former colonial power, and works closely with Mali, Gambia and Mauritania through regional bodies including ECOWAS and the African Union.

leader.name: Ana Brnabić
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Ana Brnabić is a Serbian politician serving as acting President of Serbia since 28 September 2026 and president of the National Assembly of Serbia since 2024. A member of the Serbian Progressive Party, she previously served as Prime Minister of Serbia from 2017 to 2024. She was the first woman, first openly lesbian, and longest-serving person to hold the office of prime minister. Head of government: Đuro Macut.

688.overview: Serbia's central dispute is with Kosovo, which declared independence in 2008 and which Serbia still claims as part of its territory, a position it refuses to recognise in full. Relations with Pristina remain tense over borders, Serbian-majority northern Kosovo, and the status of Serbs there. Serbia leans on Russia and China for diplomatic cover, while maintaining close ties with Hungary and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

leader.name: Patrick Herminie
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Seychellois politician.

690.overview: Seychelles has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its Indian Ocean location and its dependence on partners. Its strategic value lies in its islands along major sea lanes, and it relies on India and France for security cooperation and on the United Arab Emirates for investment. As a small state, it depends on tourism and fishing income and on its membership in the African Union, Commonwealth and SADC for diplomatic weight.

leader.name: Julius Maada Bio
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Julius Maada Wonie Bio is a Sierra Leonean politician and former military officer who has served as the 5th president of Sierra Leone since 4 April 2018. He is a retired brigadier in the Sierra Leone Army and was the military head of state of Sierra Leone from 16 January 1996 to 29 March 1996, at only 32 years old in a military junta government known as the National Provisional Ruling Council. Head of government: David Moinina Sengeh.

694.overview: Sierra Leone has few formal territorial disputes or active rivalries. Its position is shaped mainly by its neighbours Guinea and Liberia, with which it shares borders and regional ties through ECOWAS, and by reliance on Western and African partners, including the United Kingdom, for development aid and security cooperation. Its exposure to coastal insecurity, illicit trade and climate-related stress feeds into its regional diplomacy.

leader.name: Lawrence Wong
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Lawrence Wong Shyun Tsai is a Singaporean politician and civil servant who has served as the fourth prime minister of Singapore since 2024. A member of the People's Action Party, he has also served as a Member of Parliament for Marsiling–Yew Tee Group Representation Constituency since 2015 and the minister of finance since 2021. He was an MP for West Coast GRC from 2011 to 2015. Head of state: Tharman Shanmugaratnam.

702.overview: Singapore has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours, so its position is shaped by its size and vulnerability as a small island state. Its security rests on the Strait of Malacca, one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, and on defence ties with the United States and Australia. As a regional power within ASEAN, it works closely with Malaysia and Indonesia on maritime security, trade and the management of shared waters.

leader.name: Robert Fico
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Robert Fico is a Slovak politician and lawyer, who has served as the prime minister of Slovakia since 2023. Fico holds the distinction as the longest-serving prime minister in the country's history. His collective time in power spans over 13 years across four distinct mandates. Head of state: Peter Pellegrini.

703.overview: Slovakia has no territorial disputes or active rivalries of note, so its position is shaped chiefly by its membership in NATO and the European Union and by its close ties to neighbours Hungary, Austria, the Czech Republic and Poland. Its longstanding concerns are integration-related: migration pressures from the Western Balkans and beyond, and energy dependence on Russian gas and oil pipelines routed through Ukraine, which shapes its trade and supply arrangements.

leader.name: Tô Lâm
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Tô Lâm is a Vietnamese politician and former police officer who since 2024 has served as the general secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam, the highest-ranked position of the Vietnamese politics, and as the current President of Vietnam since 2026. He previously served as president from May to October 2024. Head of government: Phạm Minh Chính.

704.overview: Vietnam's central issue is its territorial dispute with China over the Paracel and Spratly Islands in the South China Sea, which both countries claim in full and which has produced maritime confrontations. Vietnam also contests parts of the sea with the Philippines, Malaysia and Taiwan. Its strategy balances this against deep economic ties with China, and it has built security partnerships with the United States, Japan, India, South Korea and Australia, while remaining a member of ASEAN.

leader.name: Janez Janša
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Ivan Janša, better known as Janez Janša, is a Slovenian politician who has served as Prime Minister of Slovenia since 2026, a position he previously held from 2004 to 2008, from 2012 to 2013 and from 2020 to 2022. Since 1993, Janša has led the Slovenian Democratic Party, which has emerged as the pre-eminent Slovenian right-wing party. Head of state: Nataša Pirc Musar.

705.overview: Slovenia has no major territorial disputes or armed rivalries, though its short border with Italy at Trieste and the Gulf of Trieste saw a long-running maritime boundary question that was settled through arbitration in 2017. Its security rests on membership of NATO and the European Union, and on close ties with Croatia, Austria, Italy and Germany. Its position is shaped mainly by regional cooperation and migration flows along the Balkan route.

leader.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud is a Somali politician who is serving as president of Somalia since 2022, his presidency being disputed since 2026. He previously held the office from 2012 to 2017. Hassan was previously a university professor and dean at SIMAD University, which he co-founded. Head of government: Mohamed Hussein Roble.

706.overview: Somalia's central geopolitical issue is its contested border with Ethiopia and the breakaway status of Somaliland, which declared independence in 1991 but is unrecognised by Somalia and most of the world. Ethiopia, a regional rival, has troops in Somalia and has signed agreements with Somaliland, while Somalia's fight against al-Shabaab militants depends on support from Kenya, Turkey, the United States and Qatar. Its position is further shaped by the African Union, the Arab League and Gulf and Turkish investment.

leader.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Matamela Cyril Ramaphosa is a South African businessman and politician who is serving as the fifth president of South Africa since 2018. A former anti-apartheid activist and trade union leader, Ramaphosa is also the president of the African National Congress. Ramaphosa rose to national prominence as secretary general of South Africa's biggest and most powerful trade union, the National Union of Mineworkers.

710.overview: South Africa has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by regional leadership and its relations with major powers. It anchors the Southern African Development Community and works with Botswana, Namibia, Mozambique and Zimbabwe on cross-border security, migration and trade. As a BRICS member it balances close economic ties with China and Russia against its traditional Western partnerships, and its large mineral exports, including gold, platinum and coal, give it weight in global markets.

leader.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of the Republic of Zimbabwe.

716.overview: Zimbabwe's geopolitical position is shaped less by territorial disputes than by its economic and political relations with its neighbours. It shares the Zambezi River and border regions with Zambia and Mozambique, and it depends on South Africa for trade, transport routes and migrant labour. Its standing within the African Union and the Southern African Development Community, along with its strained relations with Western governments over sanctions, frames its external diplomacy.

leader.name: Pedro Sánchez
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Pedro Sánchez Pérez-Castejón is a Spanish politician who has been the prime minister of Spain since 2018. A member of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party, he is also Secretary-General of the party since 2017, having previously held that office from 2014 to 2016, and is the ninth president of Socialist International since 2022. Head of state: Felipe VI.

724.overview: Spain's central geopolitical issue is its claim to Gibraltar, a British Overseas Territory at the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula that Spain has long sought to recover, while the United Kingdom holds it firmly. Spain also disputes sovereignty over the small North African enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla, which Morocco claims, and over several islets off the Moroccan coast. Its relations with Morocco and with Britain over Gibraltar shape much of its southern and western policy, and Spain relies on NATO and EU membership for its security.

leader.name: Salva Kiir
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of South Sudan since 2011.

728.overview: South Sudan's central geopolitical issue is its unresolved border with Sudan, including the oil-rich, contested Abyei area, which both sides claim and which has repeatedly flared into armed clashes. Its 2011 independence from Sudan left the two states locked in disputes over oil revenue, pipelines and borders, while internal armed conflict between government and opposition forces continues to undermine stability. It depends heavily on regional neighbours Uganda, Kenya and Ethiopia, and on the African Union and East African Community, for diplomatic backing and mediation.

leader.name: Abdel Fattah al-Burhan
leader.title: Chairman
leader.bio: Abdel Fattah al-Burhan Abdelrahman al-Burhan is a Sudanese military officer who has been the leader of Sudan since 2019. Following the Sudanese Revolution in April 2019, he was handed control of the military junta, the Transitional Military Council, a day after it was formed, due to protesters' dissatisfaction with the establishment ties of initial leader Ahmed Awad Ibn Auf. Head of government: Abdalla Hamdok.

729.overview: Sudan's central geopolitical issue is its internal armed conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces, which has fractured the state and drawn in regional patrons. Its long-running dispute with South Sudan over the oil-rich border region of Abyei and the Heglig oil field remains unresolved. Sudan leans on Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Eritrea for diplomatic and military backing, and sits within the African Union, Arab League and OIC.

732.overview: Western Sahara's central issue is its territorial dispute: Morocco controls most of the territory and claims it as its own, while the Polisario Front, backed by Algeria, seeks independence through a self-declared Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic. Morocco has built a fortified sand berm across much of the land, and a UN-monitored ceasefire has held since 1991 despite periodic clashes. Mauritania borders the territory to the south, and Algeria hosts Sahrawi refugee camps near Tindouf.

leader.name: Jennifer Geerlings-Simons
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Jennifer Geerlings-Simons is a Surinamese politician and former physician who is serving as the eleventh president of Suriname since 16 July 2025. A member of the National Democratic Party, she has been the party's president since 2024. Geerlings-Simons began her career as a physician, working as a dermatologist, and later in the National HIV/AIDS program.

740.overview: Suriname's main outstanding issue is its maritime boundary with Guyana, where both countries claim overlapping offshore areas that may hold significant oil and gas reserves. Its land border with Guyana and its boundary with French Guiana have also been subjects of long-running demarcation discussions. Suriname relies on Brazil and the Netherlands for trade, aid and close ties, and is a member of CARICOM and the Organization of American States.

leader.name: Russell Dlamini
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Russell Mmiso Dlamini is a Liswati politician. He has been serving as Prime Minister of Eswatini since 7 November 2023. Head of state: Mswati III.

748.overview: Eswatini has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours, and its position is shaped mainly by its dependence on South Africa, which surrounds it and is its main trade and transport link. Its southern African neighbour Mozambique is also a close partner, and the country relies on the Southern African Customs Union and regional bodies such as SADC and the African Union. Domestic political tensions and reliance on donor aid are the main pressures on its external relations.

leader.name: Ulf Kristersson
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Ulf Hjalmar Kristersson is a Swedish politician who has served as Prime Minister of Sweden since October 2022, and since 17 September 2026 in a caretaker capacity, following the defeat of his governing bloc in the September 2026 general election. He has been the leader of the Moderate Party since 2017. Head of state: Carl XVI Gustaf.

752.overview: Sweden's central concern is Russia, which it regards as its principal adversary, particularly in the Baltic Sea region and around the Gulf of Finland. Sweden ended a long policy of nonalignment by joining NATO, and it relies on the alliance, its partners in Finland, Norway and Denmark, and close security ties with the United States and Germany. Its position is shaped mainly by Russian military activity and Baltic maritime security rather than by any territorial dispute or armed conflict.

leader.name: Federal Council (Switzerland)
leader.title: Member
leader.bio: The Federal Council is the federal cabinet of the Swiss Confederation. Its seven members also serve as the collective head of state and government of Switzerland. Since World War II, the Federal Council is by convention a permanent grand coalition government composed of representatives of the country's major parties and language regions.

756.overview: Switzerland has no territorial disputes or active rivalries, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its neighbours and its deliberate neutrality. Its security and economy are tied closely to Germany, France, Italy and Austria, with which it shares borders and deep trade links. Its position at the centre of Europe makes migration flows, EU market access and transit routes its main external concerns.

leader.name: Ahmed al-Sharaa
leader.title: President
leader.bio: President of Syria since 2025.

760.overview: Syria's central geopolitical issue is the fragmented state itself, with the government in Damascus, Kurdish-led forces in the northeast, and Turkish-backed armed groups in the north all controlling different areas. Israel occupies the Golan Heights, which it seized in 1967 and annexed, and it conducts regular strikes against Iranian and Hezbollah targets inside Syria. Turkey's military presence in the north, aimed at the Kurdish YPG, adds to the contest over territory and borders. Syria relies heavily on Russia and Iran for military backing and on Iraq and Lebanon for trade and transit routes.

leader.name: Emomali Rahmon
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Emomali Rahmon is a Tajikistani politician who has served as the third president of Tajikistan since 1994, having previously led the country as Chairman of the Supreme Assembly from 1992 to 1994. Since 1998, he has also served as the leader of the People's Democratic Party of Tajikistan, which dominates the Parliament of Tajikistan. Head of government: Qohir Rasulzoda.

762.overview: Tajikistan's central geopolitical concern is its long, mountainous border with Afghanistan, where instability, drug trafficking and militant spillover shape its security planning. It relies on Russia, which hosts a military base and anchors its security through the CSTO, while balancing relations with Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, including unresolved border demarcation. Its ties to China, which has become a major creditor and infrastructure partner, and its dependence on Russian labour markets for migrant remittances add further pressure.

leader.name: Paetongtarn Shinawatra
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Paetongtarn Shinawatra is a Thai politician and businesswoman who served as the 31st prime minister of Thailand from 2024 until her removal from office in 2025. She led the Pheu Thai Party from 2023 until her resignation in 2025. Paetongtarn was born into the prominent Shinawatra family as the youngest child of the 23rd prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra and niece of the 28th prime minister Yingluck Shinawatra. Head of state: Vajiralongkorn.

764.overview: Thailand's central geopolitical issue is its armed conflict with Cambodia over their contested border, particularly around disputed temple areas and border demarcation. Thailand is a major non-NATO ally of the United States and a key ASEAN member, relying on Washington, Japan, China and its neighbours Malaysia and Singapore for security, trade and investment ties.

leader.name: Jean-Lucien Savi de Tové
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Jean-Lucien Kwassi Lanyo Savi de Tové is a Togolese politician and civil servant who has served as the fifth president of Togo since 3 May 2025. A member of the Pan-African Patriotic Convergence, he previously held the post of Minister of Trade, Industry and Handicrafts in the governments of Edem Kodjo and Yawovi Agboyibo from 2005 to 2007. Head of government: Faure Gnassingbé.

768.overview: Togo has no major territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours, so its position is shaped mainly by regional security and economic ties. Jihadist violence spilling over from the Sahel in its northern border areas, especially near Burkina Faso, is its most pressing concern. Togo relies on partnerships with Ghana, Benin, Burkina Faso and France, and works through ECOWAS and the African Union on regional security and trade, including the Lomé port as a transit hub for landlocked neighbours.

leader.name: Fatafehi Fakafānua
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Fatafehi Kinikinilau Lolomana‘ia Fakafānua, 8th Lord Fakafānua, is a Tongan politician and noble who has served as prime minister of Tonga since 18 December 2025. He is an extended member of the Tongan royal family. Fakafānua was first elected to the Legislative Assembly as a member of the nobility in 2008. Head of state: Tupou VI.
