776.overview: Tonga has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts, and its position is shaped chiefly by its small size and its remoteness in the South Pacific. It relies on New Zealand and Australia for security cooperation, development aid and trade links, and works within the Pacific Islands Forum and the Commonwealth. Rising sea levels and climate-related disaster risk are among its most pressing concerns.

leader.name: Kamla Persad-Bissessar
leader.title: Q30101326
leader.bio: Kamla Susheila Persad-Bissessar, often referred to by her initials KPB, is a Trinidadian politician, lawyer, and educator who has twice served as the prime minister of Trinidad and Tobago, from 2010 to 2015 and since May 2025. Head of state: Christine Kangaloo.

780.overview: Trinidad and Tobago's main geopolitical concern is its maritime boundary with Venezuela, which is contested in the Gulf of Paria and surrounding waters, and has been strained by Venezuela's territorial claims over the Essequibo region of Guyana, a neighbour with which Trinidad maintains close ties. Its position is shaped by energy: its offshore oil and gas and its role in regional trade are central to its economy. It is closely aligned with the United States and works through CARICOM, the OAS and the Commonwealth.

leader.name: Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, also known as MBZ or MbZ, is an Emirati royal and politician who has served as the third president of the United Arab Emirates and the ruler of Abu Dhabi since 2022. He was the de facto leader of the United Arab Emirates from 2014 to 2022, ruling for his brother Sheikh Khalifa. Head of government: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.

784.overview: The UAE's central geopolitical concern is its dispute with Iran over the islands of Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs, which the UAE claims and Iran administers, a question that flares in Gulf diplomacy. Iran's broader regional influence and the security of the Strait of Hormuz, through which much of the Gulf's oil passes, shape its security outlook. The UAE relies on its Gulf partnership with Saudi Arabia, its defence ties with the United States, and its oil output within OPEC for leverage.

leader.name: Kais Saied
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Kaïs Saïed is a Tunisian politician, jurist and former assistant professor of law who has served as the fifth president of Tunisia since 2019. He was president of the Tunisian Association of Constitutional Law from 1995 to 2019. Head of government: Sara Zaafarani.

788.overview: Tunisia has few longstanding territorial disputes or armed rivalries, and its position is shaped mainly by its neighbours and migration. Its border with Libya, and the instability there, drives security cooperation and concerns over smuggling and migrant flows across the Mediterranean. Tunisia relies on Europe, especially Italy and France, for trade, investment and migration partnership, and on Algeria as a close regional neighbour. Its membership in the African Union and Arab League anchors its diplomacy.

leader.name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan is a Turkish politician who has been the president of Turkey since 2014. He previously served as the 25th prime minister from 2003 to 2014 as part of the Justice and Development Party, which he co-founded in 2001. He also served as mayor of Istanbul from 1994 to 1998. Head of government: Bülend Ulusu.

792.overview: Turkey's central disputes are with Cyprus, where it backs the Turkish Cypriot north, which it recognises as a state while the Republic of Cyprus and the EU do not, and it contests maritime boundaries and gas exploration rights in the eastern Mediterranean with Greece and Cyprus. It also has a long-running rivalry with Greece over the Aegean Sea and airspace, and it maintains forces in northern Syria and northern Iraq against Kurdish armed groups. Turkey relies on its NATO membership, hosts US nuclear weapons at Incirlik, and uses its control of the Bosphorus and Dardanelles straits as leverage.

leader.name: Serdar Berdimuhamedow
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Serdar Gurbangulyýewiç Berdimuhamedow is a Turkmen politician and businessman serving as the third and current president of Turkmenistan since 2022. Berdimuhamedow had previously served in several other positions within the government of his father, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow, the long-standing authoritarian ruler of Turkmenistan.

795.overview: Turkmenistan's longstanding concerns are less about territorial disputes than about its position between Russia, Iran and Afghanistan on the Caspian Sea. It has a contested Caspian seabed boundary with Azerbaijan and Iran, and a dispute with Azerbaijan over the Kyapaz/Serdar oil field. Its leverage rests on large natural gas reserves and export routes via Russia, China, Iran and proposed pipelines through Afghanistan and Pakistan, while it balances its neutrality with ties to Turkey, Russia and China.

796.overview: The Turks and Caicos Islands are a British Overseas Territory whose central political question is its constitutional status under the United Kingdom, which retains responsibility for defence and foreign affairs. The islands rely on the UK for security and on Canada and the United States, and their economy depends heavily on tourism, financial services and migration from the Caribbean. Haiti lies to the south-west, and migration and maritime security along that route shape regional concerns.

leader.name: Feleti Teo
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Feleti Penitala Teo is a Tuvaluan politician and lawyer who is serving as the 14th prime minister of Tuvalu since 2024. He was elected to the Parliament of Tuvalu in the 2024 Tuvaluan general election, with his previous role being the executive director of the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission. Teo was appointed as prime minister on 26 February 2024, after he was elected unopposed by the parliament. Head of state: Charles III.

798.overview: Tuvalu's central concern is climate change and rising sea levels threatening its low-lying atolls, which shapes its diplomacy more than any territorial dispute. It has no contested borders or active rivalries, and relies on Australia and New Zealand for security, aid and migration pathways, while its Commonwealth and Pacific Islands Forum membership gives it a voice in regional and climate negotiations.

leader.name: Yoweri Museveni
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Yoweri Kaguta Museveni Tibuhaburwa is a Ugandan politician and former rebel leader who has served as the president of Uganda since 1986. Museveni has long been widely considered to be a dictator, with political parties being effectively banned from 1986 to 2005, and the use of political repression, lawfare and ballot stuffings to maintain power since the 2005 Ugandan multi-party referendum. Head of government: Robinah Nabbanja.

800.overview: Uganda's main external concerns are shaped by its neighbours rather than by formal territorial disputes. Its position in the Great Lakes region brings security pressure from armed groups operating across the borders of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan, and it has deployed troops in regional operations. Uganda depends on its East African Community partners, Kenya, Rwanda and Tanzania, for trade routes, and on Western and multilateral aid, while migration flows from South Sudan and the DRC shape its regional role.

leader.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Volodymyr Oleksandrovych Zelenskyy is a Ukrainian politician and former entertainer who has served as the sixth president of Ukraine since 2019. He took office five years after the start of the Russo-Ukrainian war with Russia's annexation of Crimea and invasion of the Donbas, and has continued to serve during the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine, which has been ongoing since February 2022. Head of government: Serhii Koretskyi.

804.overview: Russia's full-scale invasion has made the war in Ukraine its central issue, with Russia occupying parts of the east and south, including Crimea, which it annexed in 2014. Ukraine's dispute with Russia over these territories, alongside Belarus's role as a staging ground, shapes its security outlook. Ukraine relies heavily on the United States, the United Kingdom, Poland, Germany and France for military and financial support.

leader.name: Hristijan Mickoski
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Hristijan Mickoski is a Macedonian mechanical engineer, professor, and government official serving as Prime Minister of North Macedonia, a position he has held since June 2024. He is the party leader of VMRO-DPMNE. In 2016, Mickoski became the director of Power Plants of Macedonia, and in the period from 2015 to 2017, he was an energy advisor to prime ministers Nikola Gruevski and Emil Dimitriev. Head of state: Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova.

807.overview: North Macedonia's central geopolitical issue is its long-running name dispute with Greece, which blocked its NATO and EU accession until a 2018 agreement renamed the country. Relations with Bulgaria remain strained over historical and identity questions, and Bulgaria has contested aspects of its language and national narrative. The country relies on its NATO membership, its EU accession path, and partnerships with Albania, Serbia and the United States for security and stability.

leader.name: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Abdel Fattah Saeed Hussein Khalil el-Sisi is an Egyptian politician and retired military officer who has served as the sixth president of Egypt since 2014. Head of government: Mostafa Madbouly.

818.overview: Egypt's central geopolitical concern is the Nile: it depends on the river for nearly all its water and opposes Ethiopia's Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, a dispute over water security that has not been resolved. Egypt also faces security pressure from instability in Libya and Sudan and from militancy in the Sinai. It relies on Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and the United States for financial and military backing, and controls the Suez Canal, a key global shipping route.

leader.name: Andy Burnham
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Andrew Murray Burnham is a British politician who has served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Labour Party since July 2026. He has been Member of Parliament for Makerfield in Greater Manchester since June 2026, and was Mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to 2026; before that he was MP for Leigh from 2001 to 2017 and held several Cabinet positions. Head of state: Charles III.

826.overview: The UK's central concerns are Russian aggression in Europe, particularly the war in Ukraine, and the threat of Russian hybrid operations on British soil. It also faces strategic rivalry with China and Iran, along with North Korea, and it has no territorial disputes of its own beyond the status of Gibraltar and the Falklands, which Argentina claims. The UK relies heavily on NATO, its alliance with the United States, and its AUKUS and Five Eyes partnerships.

833.overview: The Isle of Man is a self-governing Crown dependency, not a sovereign state, and it has no territorial disputes or armed conflicts. Its position is shaped by its relationship with the United Kingdom, which handles its defence and foreign affairs, and by its reliance on financial services and tourism. Its close economic ties to the UK and Ireland, and its status as a Crown dependency outside the EU, define its external posture.

leader.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Samia Suluhu Hassan is a Tanzanian politician and the sixth president of Tanzania, serving since 19 March 2021. She is the first woman to serve in the position and previously served as vice-president of Tanzania from 2015 to 2021, from which she ascended to the presidency following the death of her predecessor, John Magufuli.

834.overview: Tanzania has no major territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours, and its position is shaped mainly by regional cooperation rather than rivalry. It is a key member of the East African Community and the Southern African Development Community, works closely with Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda and Mozambique, and draws influence from its regional ties and its role as a host for refugees from the Great Lakes region.

leader.name: Donald Trump
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Donald John Trump is an American politician, media personality, and businessman who is the 47th president of the United States. A member of the Republican Party, he served as the 45th president from 2017 to 2021. Born into a wealthy New York City family, Trump graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 1968 with a bachelor's degree in economics.

840.overview: The United States is locked in strategic rivalry with China, which claims Taiwan and has not ruled out force to take it, making the Taiwan Strait the central flashpoint. Russia and Iran pose sustained challenges, with Washington backing Ukraine and opposing Tehran's regional influence. The U.S. relies on NATO, the Quad, AUKUS and its partnerships with Japan and South Korea, while managing hostile governments in North Korea, Venezuela and Cuba.

850.overview: The U.S. Virgin Islands are an unincorporated territory of the United States, so their geopolitical position rests on that status rather than on any rival claim. Their main concerns are hurricane exposure and climate vulnerability in the Caribbean, along with dependence on U.S. federal funding, shipping links and tourism. Their relationship with Washington, including questions over political representation, shapes their standing, while neighbouring British Virgin Islands and wider Caribbean partners matter for regional cooperation.

leader.name: Ibrahim Traoré
leader.title: Military leader
leader.bio: Military leader of Burkina Faso since 2022. Head of government: Apollinaire J. Kyélem de Tambèla.

854.overview: Burkina Faso's central security concern is the jihadist insurgency in its north and east, linked to al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates that operate across the Sahel borders with Mali and Niger. The military government has grown closer to Russia and to its Sahel neighbours in the Alliance of Sahel States, while tensions with France and Western partners have sharpened. Its landlocked position makes its trade routes to Ivorian and Ghanaian ports strategically important.

leader.name: Yamandú Orsi
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Yamandú Ramón Antonio Orsi Martínez is a Uruguayan politician and history teacher who has been the 43rd president of Uruguay since March 2025. A member of the left-wing Movement of Popular Participation, the main faction of the Broad Front party, he served as intendant of the Canelones Department from 2015 to February 2020, and a second term from November 2020 to 2024.

858.overview: Uruguay has no active territorial disputes or armed rivalries, so its geopolitical position is shaped mainly by its neighbours and trade. Its border with Brazil and Argentina is settled, and its security depends on regional cooperation through Mercosur, the Organization of American States, and close ties with Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay. Its position as a small agricultural exporter makes it sensitive to trade access and regional economic conditions.

leader.name: Shavkat Mirziyoyev
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Shavkat Miromonovich Mirziyoyev is an Uzbek politician who has served as the second president of Uzbekistan since 2016. A member of the Uzbekistan Liberal Democratic Party, he served as the third prime minister under President Islam Karimov from 2003 to 2016. Mirziyoyev has also served as chairman of the Organization of Turkic States since 2022.

860.overview: Uzbekistan's position is shaped less by territorial disputes than by its landlocked location and its balancing among larger powers. Its main concerns are instability in neighbouring Afghanistan and water-sharing tensions over the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers with Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Kazakhstan. It works closely with Russia, China and Turkey, while maintaining regional ties through the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and the Commonwealth of Independent States.

leader.name: Delcy Rodríguez
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Acting President of Venezuela since 2026.

862.overview: Venezuela's central geopolitical dispute is its claim to the Essequibo region, roughly two-thirds of neighbouring Guyana, which it contests under the 1899 arbitral award and which has become a major source of tension with Guyana and its US backing. Venezuela's rivalry with the United States, which has imposed sanctions and backs Guyana, shapes much of its external position. It relies on Russia, China, Cuba, Iran and Nicaragua for diplomatic cover, investment and security cooperation, while its oil reserves give it leverage through its OPEC membership.

leader.name: Fiamē Naomi Mataʻafa
leader.title: Prime Minister
leader.bio: Afioga Fiamē Naomi Mataʻafa is a Samoan politician and High Chief who served as the seventh Prime Minister of Samoa from 2021 to 2025. She has led the Samoa Uniting Party since 2025. The daughter of Samoa's first prime minister Fiamē Mataʻafa Faumuina Mulinuʻu II, Mataʻafa is the first woman to serve as Samoa's head of government. Head of state: Tuimalealiʻifano Vaʻaletoʻa Sualauvi II.

882.overview: Samoa has no territorial disputes or active rivalries, so its geopolitical position is shaped by its small size, its Pacific neighbours and its close ties to larger partners. It relies heavily on New Zealand and Australia for aid, trade access, security cooperation and migration pathways. Its influence is exercised mainly through the Pacific Islands Forum and the Commonwealth, where climate change and ocean security are its primary concerns.

leader.name: Rashad al-Alimi
leader.title: حسان حسين محمد السعيدي الجمهورية اليمنية
leader.bio: Rashad Muhammad al-Alimi is a Yemeni politician who is serving as the president of the Presidential Leadership Council since 2022. Head of government: Salem Saleh bin Braik.

887.overview: Yemen's central issue is its civil war, with Houthi forces holding the capital Sanaa and much of the north against the internationally recognised government, which Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have long backed. The Houthis have fired missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia, Israel and shipping in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait, drawing US and Israeli strikes. The southern separatist movement, which seeks an independent South Yemen, adds a further rift, while the Gulf Cooperation Council and Oman shape its diplomacy.

leader.name: Hakainde Hichilema
leader.title: President
leader.bio: Hakainde Hichilema, often known by his initials HH and the nickname "Bally", is a Zambian businessman, farmer, and politician who is the seventh and current president of Zambia since 24 August 2021. Since the death of Guy Scott in 2026, he is the only living person who has been president of Zambia. Head of government: Edgar Lungu.

894.overview: Zambia has no active territorial disputes or armed conflicts with neighbours, so its position is shaped mainly by regional ties and resource exposure. It is a member of the Southern African Development Community and works closely with Zimbabwe, Malawi, Tanzania and South Africa on trade, transport and border security. Its copper and cobalt output links it to global commodity markets and to China, a major investor and buyer, while debt restructuring and dependence on foreign lenders remain key pressures.
